title: Sales Associate (Part-Time), Los Angeles
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.




ALSO is looking for a Part-Time Sales Associate to support the launch and growth of our brand in/around Los Angeles. This is a field-based, customer-facing role that works closely with and reports to the Market Manager to bring ALSO to life through mobile demos, retail experiences, and community activations. You’ll be on the front lines—introducing customers to our vehicles, delivering exceptional experiences, and helping build the foundation of ALSO’s presence in Los Angeles.

This role is ideal for someone who is energetic, people-oriented, and excited to be part of an early-stage brand with room to grow.

 

What You Will Do

Customer Experience & Sales Support

 - Deliver engaging, high-quality customer experiences in both mobile and fixed retail environments.

 - Educate customers on ALSO vehicles, features, and benefits, guiding them through demo rides and early purchase consideration.

 - Support local sales goals by converting interest into qualified leads and sales.

 - Share customer feedback and insights with the Market Manager to improve execution and experiences.

Mobile Demo & Event Support

 - Assist with the setup, execution, and breakdown of mobile demo experiences and local activation events, including driving the custom Rivian EV van to/from events.

 - Safely operate and maintain the local demo fleet, ensuring vehicles are clean, charged, and customer-ready.

 - Represent ALSO at community events, pop-ups, and partner activations.

Retail Store Operations (in applicable markets, over time)

 - Support daily retail hub operations, including opening and closing procedures, merchandising, and general upkeep.

 - Deliver best-in-class customer service and demonstrate active selling skills.

 - Help create a welcoming, on-brand environment that reflects ALSO’s premium and playful ethos.

Operational Support

 - Follow operational, safety, and compliance processes as directed by the Market Manager and/or Market Coordinator.
   
   
   

What You Will Bring

 - 1+ years of experience in retail, events, sales, hospitality, brand ambassador, or customer-facing roles.

 - A positive, proactive attitude and willingness to jump in wherever needed - you actively engage in your professional development.

 - Strong interpersonal and communication skills—you enjoy talking to people, telling a compelling story, and actively selling products and services.

 - Ability to work in a dynamic, field-based environment, including weekends and events - you have a flexible work style and enjoy variety in your work schedule.

 - Interest in cycling, electric vehicles and/or innovative consumer brands - your enthusiasm for our brand is infectious!

 - Ability to work collaboratively while also taking direction and feedback well - you are a charismatic and fun team player!

 - A strong connection to, knowledge of and comfort riding a bike in Los Angeles is a plus!

 - Qualify as an authorized driver, meaning you are at least 21 years of age, have a valid U.S. driver’s license with a minimum of three (3) years of licensed driving experience, and can successfully complete a background screening and motor vehicle review - because you’ll be driving our demo van and fleet of bikes to meet customers where they like to ride!
   
   
   

This position offers an hourly pay rate of $21.00 per hour and is eligible to participate in the sales incentive program in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan. This role is expected to work approximately 20–24 hours per week. As a part-time position working fewer than 30 hours per week, this role is not eligible for company-sponsored benefits.

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

The Director, Factory of the Future, leads AbbVie’s global strategy, design standards, and delivery of next-generation factories and manufacturing operations that leverage Industry 4.0/5.0, robotics, automation, and AI. The Director owns the Factory of the Future vision and roadmap across biotechnology, aseptic manufacturing, packaging, medical device, and chemical production, and leads a team of senior engineers and technical leaders who develop reference designs, run pilots, and enable deployment into new facilities and major site transformations. This role partners with Operations leadership, Engineering, Quality, PDS&T, Supply Chain, BTS, and Security to ensure future factories are safe, compliant, flexible, and highly automated, and deliver measurable gains in quality, speed, and cost.

Factory of the Future strategy: Define and own the multi-year Factory of the Future vision, technology roadmap, and investment case, aligned to Operations, network, and enterprise AI and digital strategies.
Network and capital alignment: Partner with Global Engineering, Manufacturing, and Finance to embed future-factory design principles and technology choices into the capital plan, site master plans, and new-facility business cases.
Design and Technology Leadership
Reference designs and standards: Establish global reference designs, design standards, and technology platforms for aseptic and biologics manufacturing, packaging, device assembly, and chemical production, including modular, flexible, and continuous concepts.
Automation, robotics, and AI: Direct the evaluation, piloting, and scale-up of robotics, autonomous material handling, vision inspection, digital twins, advanced process control, and AI-enabled operations, in partnership with BTS and Operations AI.
Technical governance: Provide design authority and review for major capital projects; ensure cGMP, Annex 1, data integrity, device regulations, EHS, and OT/IT cybersecurity requirements are built in from concept stage.

Leadership and Ecosystem
Team leadership: Build, lead, and develop a global team of principal and senior principal engineers and technical specialists; create a pipeline of future-factory talent.
External engagement: Develop strategic relationships with equipment OEMs, automation integrators, technology startups, academia, and industry bodies (e.g., ISPE) to benchmark and access emerging capabilities.

Experience developing and leading high-performing technical teams, including senior technical talent.

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
*Candidate should live within the territory. The territory includes New York and New Jersey.*
The Oncology Nurse Educator (ONE) will be responsible for proactively engaging with allied healthcare professionals to provide product and disease education, in support of before, during and after patient management on approved therapies in our Solid Tumor portfolio. The ONE will focus on providing ongoing education and resources related to patient management, dosing and administration, and side effect management. The ONE will collaborate with other field teams within ways of working guidelines to ensure education support for allied healthcare clinicians.
The Oncology Nurse Educator (ONE) interacts with allied healthcare clinicians in key targeted accounts and provide clinical in-services and education. The ONE identifies educational needs and expands disease state awareness, initiating and managing patients on a therapy, understanding of symptom management and appropriate patient identification through these educational interactions within a defined geographical region.
Responsibilities
Serve as a strategic education leader across academic and community oncology accounts by way of: Proactive and reactive education with approved resources to the patient care team members.
Develops a customized educational plan through the analysis of account dynamics and clinical insights that meet the patient care team’s needs and clinical challenges.
Educate on the preparation and administration requirements of TA products; and adverse event mitigation, monitoring, and management.
Interpret and communicate relevant clinical education topics to diverse audiences as per materials approved for the role.
Educate on disease state awareness, including clinical and operational aspects of appropriate patient diagnosis.
Provide education programs through 1:1 presentations/in-services and other methods expressly approved, which may include round-table discussions, and podium presentations.
Educate patient care teams about the infusion process associated with the product.
Utilize strategic questioning and active listening to routinely document and share clinical insights.
Attend and provide clinical information and/or presentations at internal national, regional, and local meetings.
Provide staff support as appropriate at exhibit booths and displays.
Provide support to enhance training initiatives clinically and improve the clinical competencies of the internal sales team.
As deemed appropriate, collaborates across internal functional areas as it relates to the Oncology business (e.g., sales, marketing, clinical operations, medical, clinical value & evidence)
Potentially provide education to patients in patient advocacy meeting settings using materials and messaging tailored and approved for use with such an audience.
Bachelor’s degree required (Nursing or NP preferred)
Master's level education preferred
Three or more years of combined clinical experience and/or pharmaceutical sales, clinical educator, or medical affairs experience (Oncology preferred) Experience working in or supporting patients and HCPs in the infusion center setting, including the development/implementation of chemotherapy/biologics infusion procedures and protocols for therapy administration and patient safety monitoring is preferred.
Excellent communication(s), objective setting, influencing, business acumen, and analytical skills
Demonstrated experience adapting to change and embracing learning
Demonstrated experience interpreting clinical and pharmacoeconomic data
Recognizes evolving shifts in oncology market trends and respective effects on provider and patient
Success operating within a cross-functional team
Proficiency in Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, and other relevant applications
The individual must be able to travel 50% of the time, including the ability to travel overnight and occasionally on weekends
Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment
Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements

As Principal Data Scientist I, you are a technical leader and lead data scientist who design, build, and oversee bioinformatics platforms and data systems that streamline, integrate, and standardize scientific workflows across R&D. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of how scientists work and what they need, then translate that into systems and data solutions with the business partner organizations they support. Extensive, progressively responsible experience in aseptic manufacturing, engineering, including leadership of complex manufacturing equipment or facility programs.
Hands-on leadership experience across equipment design reviews, vendor and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, and manufacturing start-up.

Experience implementing advanced manufacturing technologies and translating project delivery knowledge into sustainable operational capability.

The Senior IT Change Management Lead provides functional leadership for the execution, governance, and continuous improvement of AbbVie’s IT Change Management process. Lead day-to-day operational execution of the IT Change Management process, ensuring consistent application of established policies, procedures, and governance requirements.
Provide functional leadership across Normal, Expedited, Emergency, and Standard Change processes.
Lead structured reviews of change records for completeness, quality, risk, readiness, and alignment with process requirements.
Identify and address unauthorized, latent, urgent, miscategorized, or otherwise non-compliant changes, escalating material or recurring concerns as appropriate.
Analyze recurring process and change-quality issues and recommend improvements to governance, guidance, training, controls, or system capabilities.
CAB, Change Quality, and Post-Implementation Governance
Lead operational preparation and readiness activities for Change Advisory Board meetings, including pre-CAB reviews, agenda readiness, change-owner follow-up, and post-CAB action tracking.
Partner with change owners, technical teams, and technology leaders to resolve readiness or documentation gaps before governance review.
Provide particular focus on Medium- and High-risk changes to ensure appropriate risk, impact, testing, implementation, validation, and recovery considerations are documented and understood.
Coordinate Post-Implementation Review activities for applicable changes, including candidate identification, completion tracking, stakeholder follow-up, and documentation of outcomes.
Analyze failed changes, PIR outcomes, and recurring quality or compliance issues to identify systemic trends and opportunities for corrective or preventive improvement.
Reporting, ServiceNow, and Continuous Improvement
Develop, maintain, and enhance Change Management reports, dashboards, metrics, and recurring operational summaries.
Analyze trends in change performance, including change success, aging records, failed changes, PIR activity, process compliance, and change-quality indicators.
Translate operational data into actionable insights and recommendations for Change Management leadership, technology teams, and governance stakeholders.
Partner with ServiceNow, Service Management, Quality, and process stakeholders to define and support Change Management enhancements, including requirements, testing, validation, communication, and adoption.
Identify opportunities to simplify or automate recurring reporting, notifications, workflow activities, and operational follow-up.
Support the continued modernization, governance, and recertification of Standard Changes and identification of repeatable activities appropriate for Standard Change.
Knowledge Management and Stakeholder Leadership
Maintain and improve Change Management knowledge articles, procedures, job aids, standards, and supporting process documentation.
Ensure Change Management documentation remains aligned with current ServiceNow workflows, approval models, governance requirements, and operating practices.
Develop communications, guidance, and training materials supporting process changes and recurring change-quality needs.
Serve as a trusted Change Management advisor to technical teams, Service Management, Quality, governance partners, and business stakeholders.
Provide clear guidance on Change Management requirements, change readiness, documentation, approvals, governance expectations, and ServiceNow usage.
Influence cross-functional stakeholders to address identified risks and process gaps and escalate significant or recurring concerns when appropriate.
Provide functional guidance to Change Management analysts, contractors, or other operational resources as needed.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, IT Service Management, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
7+ years of relevant experience in Information Technology, IT Service Management, technology operations, governance, or a related discipline, with demonstrated experience supporting or leading IT Change Management activities.
Demonstrated knowledge of IT Change Management principles and practices, including change risk and impact assessment, approval and governance processes, implementation readiness, post-implementation review, and change quality.
Experience working with enterprise ITSM platforms and processes, including change workflows, approvals, reporting, and operational record management.
Demonstrated ability to lead operational activities and influence outcomes across technical, operational, Quality, and leadership stakeholder groups without direct authority.
Experience analyzing operational data, identifying trends or process gaps, and translating findings into practical process, governance, reporting, or automation improvements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear guidance, challenge gaps constructively, facilitate discussions, and communicate effectively with both technical teams and leadership.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate effectively in a complex, cross-functional environment.

ITIL Foundation certification or advanced ITIL/IT Service Management certification.
Hands-on experience with ServiceNow Change Management, including workflows, approvals, Standard Changes, reporting, dashboards, and change lifecycle management.
Experience supporting or facilitating Change Advisory Board (CAB) activities, including readiness reviews, high-risk change review, stakeholder coordination, and follow-up.
Experience working in a regulated pharmaceutical, healthcare, life sciences, or similarly compliance-driven environment, including interaction with Quality or audit requirements.
Experience with Post-Implementation Reviews (PIRs), failed-change analysis, corrective actions, or continuous-improvement activities.
Experience developing and maintaining knowledge articles, procedures, job aids, process standards, or training materials.
Experience with ServiceNow reporting, Power BI, Excel, or similar analytics and visualization tools.
Experience identifying or implementing workflow automation, reporting automation, notifications, or other improvements that reduce manual operational effort.

Purpose
The Senior Manager, Strategic Initiatives – US M&A Operations independently leads complex, cross-functional initiatives that enable the operational execution of US acquisitions, integrations, divestitures, carve-outs, and operating-model changes. The role translates transaction and business objectives into actionable, integrated plans; establishes governance and operating cadence to drive decisions; and provides executive-ready visibility to progress, risks, dependencies, and outcomes.
Working across US and global functions, this leader brings structure and practical problem-solving across the execution lifecycle—from diligence and planning through Day 1, transition services agreement (TSA) execution and exit, stabilization, and hypercare. Improve M&A operations playbooks, templates, dashboards, metrics, and practices by applying lessons learned. Support other enterprise-wide or strategic initiatives as defined by Strategic Initiatives leadership.

Experience in management consulting, M&A integration or separation, transformation, operations, or related strategic execution.

Strategic execution; enterprise influence; operational rigor; people and matrix leadership; learning agility. AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.
Create a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.
Embrace the ideas of others, nurture innovation and manage innovation to reality.

description:

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to advance quantitative bioimaging capabilities in support of immunology discovery research. In this role, you will work within a cross-functional team with access to multiple microscopy modalities, complex in vitro models, multimodal biological datasets, and advanced computational infrastructure.
You will develop and apply quantitative imaging, computer-vision, and machine-learning approaches to characterize cellular and tissue phenotypes, support the development of biological models, including co-cultures, organ-on-chip systems, organoids, and tissue explants, and generate insights that advance immunology discovery programs. This role combines hands-on delivery of robust, reproducible image-analysis workflows with the evaluation and application of advanced AI/ML approaches, including biomedical image segmentation, representation learning, foundation models, and scalable computational workflows. You will partner closely with wet-lab scientists, imaging specialists, computational scientists, and other subject-matter experts to translate biological questions into rigorous and impactful analysis strategies.
The role sits at the intersection of biology, bioengineering, microscopy, and computational science. Candidates with combined expertise in two or more of these areas are especially encouraged to apply.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, optimize, and apply imaging assays and quantitative image-analysis workflows for 2D and 3D cellular and tissue models to characterize cellular and other complex biological phenotypes.
Collaborate with wet-lab assay scientists, imaging specialists, and computational scientists from experimental and assay design through image acquisition, analysis, validation, and data delivery.
Extract biologically meaningful, multiparametric features from high-content imaging datasets and use them to characterize disease-relevant phenotypes, mechanisms, and treatment responses.
Apply statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods to identify candidate imaging biomarkers and relate imaging phenotypes to molecular, functional, and other biological readouts.
Contribute to the integration of imaging data with multimodal datasets, including molecular, single-cell, spatial, or perturbational data, where appropriate.
Establish quality-control and evaluation frameworks to assess image and assay quality, distinguish biological signal from technical artifacts, and define data-quality criteria, acceptance thresholds, and analytical limitations.
Maintain clear experimental and analytical records; analyze, visualize, and present results rigorously to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Communicate methods, assumptions, results, uncertainties, and limitations effectively to cross-functional project teams.
Stay current with advances in quantitative bioimaging, image analysis, computer vision, and AI/ML for biological imaging, and evaluate opportunities to incorporate relevant approaches into team workflows.
Basic Qualifications
BS, MS, or PhD in engineering, biophysics, computational biology, imaging science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline, with typically 10-12+ (BS), 8-10+ (MS), or 0-4+ (PhD) years experience.
Demonstrated experience developing quantitative image-analysis or computational solutions involving one or more of the following: image segmentation, feature extraction, phenotypic profiling, object classification, or analysis of high-content imaging data.
Experience with at least one relevant imaging modality or assay type, such as confocal microscopy, high-content imaging, or cell painting.
Ability to assess image quality, recognize common imaging artifacts, and interpret biologically meaningful phenotypes.
Working knowledge of machine-learning or deep-learning approaches for biological imaging, with the ability to understand model behavior, assess performance, and contribute to appropriate evaluation strategies.
Proficiency with the Python data-science ecosystem, including NumPy, pandas, Polars, scikit-learn, and/or PyTorch.
Strong biological grounding, attention to experimental rigor, and demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with wet-lab and computational colleagues.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain methods, results, assumptions, and limitations to diverse audiences.

Experience working with complex in vitro models, such as organoids, organ-on-chip systems, co-cultures, tissue explants, or other advanced in vitro platforms.
Experience with classical bioimage-analysis tools such as CellProfiler, scikit-image, ImageJ/Fiji, or comparable platforms.
Exposure to deep-learning, self-supervised learning, foundation-model, embedding-based, or multimodal AI approaches for biological imaging.
Peer-reviewed publications, patents, conference presentations, or other demonstrated scientific contributions in quantitative bioimaging, computer vision, computational biology, bioengineering, or a related field.

title: Global Alliance Director, AWS
description:
About the Role
The Global Alliance Director, AWS owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and AWS. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market (GTM) strategy, expand customer relationships and AWS Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and AWS, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.
This is a build role. AWS’s partner ecosystem is early, and its programs are still being designed. You will work across AWS, technology partners, and systems integrators (SIs), whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align, and you will help shape how new technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through AWS field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.
Governance and Operating Cadence
Lead the alliance operating rhythm: annual business planning, executive business reviews (EBRs), and quarterly and monthly business reviews (QBRs, MBRs).
Develop and manage annual business plans, growth initiatives, and partnership objectives with Adobe and AWS leaders.
Build scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting.
Maintain executive engagement plans, stakeholder maps, governance frameworks, and action tracking.
Prepare executive-ready materials, including strategic updates, account reviews, business cases, win stories, and operating plans.
Performance and Measurement
Own executive dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and performance reporting for both leadership teams.
Define, track, and report alliance KPIs: revenue influence, AWS consumption, Marketplace performance, co-sell activity, customer adoption, migration outcomes, and executive engagement.
Monitor partnership health, flag risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to accelerate growth, drawing on data from sales, finance, marketing, product, engineering, and customer success.
Drive operational excellence through process improvement, reporting automation, and business insights.
Field Activation and Marketplace Growth
Expand AWS Marketplace adoption and manage incentive programs, sponsorships, funding, and co-sell benefits.
Activate partner field teams around Adobe priorities and strategic accounts to accelerate adoption of Adobe’s priority joint solutions and relevant third-party partner solutions.
Deliver enablement programs, workshops, and GTM guidance so Adobe solutions are positioned effectively in AWS customer conversations, driving consumption through Adobe workloads and modern workplace initiatives.
Support regional sales leadership meetings, pipeline management, reporting, and field enablement alongside the Adobe AWS Alliance team.
Marketing and Thought Leadership
Work with Adobe and AWS sales and marketing teams to develop assets, events, and customer programs.
Support customer references, success stories, analyst engagements, and executive communications.
Present at industry events, customer workshops, and alliance forums, positioning Adobe as a strategic cloud, AI, and digital workspace partner in the AWS ecosystem.
Cross-Functional and Product Alignment
Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-AWS partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.
Work with product management and engineering to align Adobe and AWS roadmaps and secure opportunities and funding for integration, innovation, and joint solutions.
Represent customer and AWS requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.
Qualifications
Education: MBA or equivalent practical experience.
Experience: 15+ years in global technology partner management, GTM, and partner sales leadership, working directly with enterprise customers, cloud service providers, C-level executives, and sales leaders.
Industry knowledge: Enterprise software sales and operations, competitive landscapes, and cloud marketplace business models.
Alliance expertise: Deep knowledge of alliance management, co-sell metrics and motions, and partner programs, ideally within the AWS ecosystem.
Hyperscaler partnerships: Experience developing GTM strategy and co-sell programs with the largest hyperscalers.
Strategic agreements: Experience planning and executing multi-year partner sales and product agreements.
Influence and collaboration: Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and drive execution across matrix organizations, including sales, product, and marketing.
Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.
Adaptability: Comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments across time zones, with a focus on measurable outcomes.
Travel: Willingness to travel as needed to support partner and business priorities.

description:

Creative work increasingly starts inside an AI assistant, not only inside an app. Adobe is building a unified plugin and skills that brings Firefly, Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere, Express, Acrobat and more into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and what's to come. Own the plugin architecture. Define the tools, resources, and UI contracts that expose Adobe capabilities to third-party hosts. Keep one design working across hosts with different capabilities and harnesses, while it connects seamlessly with the Adobe ecosystem.
Lead partner engineering. Run the technical relationship with partner companies and internal product teams. Shape integration contracts and pick the technical bets that differentiate Adobe.

Build evaluation suites and compatibility layers so reliability holds as hosts change. Production work with the Model Context Protocol: tool design, servers and clients, auth flows, and versioning.
Familiarity with agent harnesses and generative UI such as A2UI, and with how large language models behave in production.

Clear writer, speaker, and presenter. Sharp in a technical review, at ease in an executive briefing or a standards group, and compelling on stage with a live demo of what the plugin can do.

Your work will help the organization measure AI adoption and spending, understand the economics of its products, and connect enterprise application data to meaningful business and operational insights.
You will own complex data engineering projects from requirements gathering and technical design through implementation, validation, and production operations. Working closely with stakeholders and engineering partners, you will build maintainable data models and pipelines that accommodate new AI tools, products, cost categories, and enterprise systems while preserving clear definitions, traceability, and reliable historical data.
Operating in an ecosystem that includes petabyte-scale datasets, you will improve correctness, freshness, performance, and cost efficiency. You will build reusable components that simplify source onboarding and reduce duplicated logic. Through design reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentorship, you will help strengthen the team’s engineering practices and contribute to Airbnb’s broader data community.

Implement automated testing, reconciliation, anomaly detection, and monitoring to protect data accuracy, completeness, and availability.
Plan and execute safe migrations and historical backfills through dependency analysis, validation, controlled cutovers, and recovery planning.

title: Inventory Health Program Lead, Materials Allocation & Planning
description:
AWS runs the largest cloud infrastructure in the world, backed by billions of dollars in hardware inventory. We’re looking for an Inventory Health Program Lead to turn excess and obsolete (E&O) hardware into value. You’ll build secondary supply channels that don’t exist at scale today, structure commercial deals with suppliers and partners, and work with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts into current and future builds. This is a 2–3 year effort across every commodity family. The long-term goal is to change how AWS sources and commits to hardware, so E&O exposure is prevented upstream instead of cleaned up afterward.
In this role, you will:
Build a program from scratch that owns the full lifecycle of inventory health — from proactive exposure monitoring and inspection through financial alignment, cost recovery, and commercial disposition. Establish governance, standardized processes, and executive review cadences across a global network of integrator and ODM sites spanning multiple commodity families.
Drive measurable outcomes tied directly to financial planning cycles, with reduction targets tracked monthly, quarterly, and annually. Own the automation roadmap that replaces manual, fragmented workflows with scalable, system-driven execution
This isn't a role where you inherit a playbook — you're writing it. You'll work across engineering, finance, operations, and manufacturing partners to bring structure and accountability to a space with massive impact on AWS's cost structure. If you thrive on ambiguity, love building from zero, and want your work to be visible at the highest levels of the organization, this is the role.
Key job responsibilities
Design, negotiate and scale new reuse, resale and recovery channels, including secondary-market buyers, ODM/integrator buy-backs and cross-platform redeployment.
Structure strategic buy transactions with suppliers and partners on excess positions, covering returns, rebalancing and repurposing.
Work with hardware engineering to qualify excess components into current and future platforms through BOM cross-referencing and fungibility analysis, shaping platform design and sourcing decisions.
Feed recovery insights back into category strategy so future sourcing and commitment decisions reduce E&O exposure.
Own a multi-year E&O reduction strategy across all commodity families, with targets built into OP1/OP2 and tracked monthly, quarterly and annually.
Set up the governance, standard disposition processes and executive review cadences that support channel execution across global integrator and ODM sites.
Define the automation roadmap and KPIs that show leadership how much is being recovered, how fast cycles are moving and where the risk is.
A day in the life
Negotiating terms with a secondary-market buyer or an ODM on a buy-back of excess material.
Working through a BOM cross-reference with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts for a new platform build.
Modeling the recovery value of different disposition paths (redeploy, resell, return, write off) and taking a recommendation to Finance.
Partnering with commodity managers to change commit strategy based on where exposure keeps building up.
Presenting channel performance and E&O reduction progress to senior leadership
About the team
You'll join a team within AWS Infrastructure Supply Chain that ensures the right hardware is planned, allocated, and positioned across one of the largest global supply chains in the world. This role stands up a new commercial function focused on recovering value from hardware inventory. You'll have the autonomy to build new channels and the visibility to shape how AWS sources hardware. We own the end-to-end material lifecycle — from supply planning and allocation through inventory health management across a global network of manufacturing sites. We build from zero, operate at massive scale with startup energy, and sit at the center of engineering, finance, and operations. Every person has outsized impact. This role stands up a new function focused on inventory health — you'll have the autonomy to build it and the visibility to drive change.

- 5+ years of program or project management experience, or a MBA and 5+ years of working cross functionally across several teams experience
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences
- Bachelor's degree, or BS degree
- Experience structuring and negotiating commercial agreements with suppliers, partners or buyers

- Experience working with hardware engineering on component qualification, BOMs or platform design
- Financial modeling or P&L experience (recovery value, reserves, write-offs)
- SQL or Python for data analysis
- Experience automating manual processes at scale

title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
• Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
• Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
• Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

Influence without authority across organizations. Build and hold alignment with Amazon payments teams, Prime, Legal, Finance, Accounting and external partners, each with their own priorities and their own roadmaps.
Write the documents that move the company. Narratives, PRFAQs, and the operating plan sections for this domain.

description:

Translate legal interpretations into implementable technical requirements.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM), Items and Offers Platform - Offers
description:
Our systems are at the core of Amazon.com. We serve the product and offering catalog containing billions of records, and we are the authority for product information, including availability and price. Our systems respond to billions of requests per day that power the Amazon shopping experiences and other customer interfaces, such as Amazon Shopping App, Kindle, Wholefoods, Amazon Fresh and Amazon Alexa. We get more traffic than most other Amazon systems and most requests are handled within a few milliseconds.
We are regularly challenged by new business use-cases that bring in high levels of ambiguity and competing priorities. Our team has been instrumental in launching high-impact customer features, such as "Buy For Me" that helps customers discover and seamlessly purchase select products from other brands’ sites if those items are not currently sold in Amazon’s store. We also helped launch "Amazon Now", with its own shopping experience, search, cart, and checkout so customers can get essential everyday items delivered to them in minutes. By building segmented offers, we helped Amazon provide sub-same-day delivery to our customers and achieve the fastest delivery speeds in the US last year. We are also tackling the challenge of implementing regional pricing that scales to meet the unique needs of diverse markets, ensuring our customers receive fair and competitive prices no matter where they are located.
While large-scale, high-throughput, low-latency systems are common at Amazon, the services operated by this team differentiate themselves by being the top-traffic serving systems, serving hundreds of trillions of requests per day, supporting 1 billion transactions per second in single-digit millisecond latencies. These systems source data from many data sources and execute logic to determine buyability of the items in the Amazon catalog, which is consumed by hundreds of systems.
In this role, you will participate in all parts of the software development process, from collaborating with customers to understand their needs, to design, to executing that design in a scalable and extensible way. You will have the opportunity to solve hard problems and help the business grow. Successful candidates are passionate about translating high-level, ambiguous business goals to software platforms that enable multiple businesses.
Key job responsibilities
You must be able to:
- Interact with Project Sponsors, other Technical Program Managers, and multiple development teams to define and deliver complex cross-functional projects.
- Drive large scale projects spanning teams across Amazon from inception to conclusion, create the roadmap, define user stories, research appropriate technical solutions.
- Clearly communicate roadmap, plans and project status to management and key technical and business stakeholders.
- Work closely with the software development team on delivering high-quality solutions, and provide guidance regarding architecture, design, and priorities.
- Engage with other teams across Amazon to evangelize the team and your projects, to build relationships and help identify existing technologies that can be leveraged to meet your team’s goals.
- Identify, assess and mitigate risks, provide escalation management, anticipate and make trade-offs balancing the business needs versus constraints.
- Create, maintain and disseminate project information to stakeholders.

- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

AWS operates the world's largest fleet of Storage servers powering S3 at cloud scale. Our team takes these platforms from design into high-volume production, owning the manufacturing processes, test strategies, and quality systems that determine whether a new server ships on time and at the right quality. If you want to own how the hardware that frontier models train on actually gets built, this is the role.
We are seeking a Sr Manufacturing Product Engineer to drive New Product Introduction (NPI) manufacturing and quality for Storage server platforms, from early design engagement through volume production. You will define manufacturing processes, test flows, and quality controls, serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM partners, and ensure products are optimized for manufacturability and launched at exceptional quality.
What You Will Do
You will own how a new Storage platform is manufactured. You will engage with hardware design early to influence testability and manufacturability, define the manufacturing test strategy and quality plan, and drive the process from prototype through Pilot and volume ramp. You will run NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments before design freeze, lead design reviews, and drive root cause corrective action on manufacturing blockers and quality escapes. When a platform ramps to volume with high first-pass yield and no quality escapes reaching the fleet, that is your impact.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models train on the hardware you help build. You will see your process and test decisions scale across a large fleet of servers, and you will work at the point where design meets the factory floor. The team is deeply technical and high-trust, and you own manufacturing outcomes end to end from design engagement through volume production.
The Ideal Candidate
You think across the full manufacturing stack, from SMT assembly and test coverage to line balance, yield, and quality systems. You are as comfortable in a DFx review reading gerber files as you are on an ODM floor debugging a failing test station. You drive decisions with data, hold manufacturing partners to a high bar, and bring structured problem-solving and disciplined change management to a fast-moving NPI environment. You mentor junior engineers, contribute to hiring, and raise the manufacturing engineering bar for the team.
Key job responsibilities
Design for Manufacturability & Risk
- Perform NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments and carry-over analysis to identify and mitigate manufacturing risks before design freeze
- Participate in DFx reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT) leveraging mechanical CAD models, gerber files, and mock-up samples, driving design improvements in partnership with hardware engineering
- Lead DFMEA/PFMEA reviews and develop process flow diagrams and quality control plans
NPI Manufacturing & Test Strategy
- Own end-to-end NPI manufacturing execution for Storage server platforms across engineering phases and Pilot builds
- Define the manufacturing test strategy including test flows, coverage, duration, fixture requirements such as in circuit tests (ICT), board functional test (BFT) and system-level tests
- Own Contract Manufacturer enablement including BOM requirements, assembly workflows, testing protocols, and tooling specifications
- Research automation techniques and develop new tests and systems to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce test dwell time
Quality & Continuous Improvement
- Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers and quality escapes
- Execute test rack inspections and quality checklists; issue quality alerts, deviations, and ship-holds as required
- Own manufacturing quality metrics and drive yield improvement, and cost optimization through process and automation engineering
Capacity & Production Ramp
- Create manufacturing capacity plans with simulations across build phases; conduct line balance and cycle time analysis to maximize throughput
- Provide on-site ODM support during critical builds and production ramp
- Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams on Storage module integration, thermal validation, and manufacturing requirements
Cross-Team Collaboration
- Serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM/CM partners
- Manage manufacturing requirements, scope, schedules, and deliverables across engineering teams, suppliers, and partners
- Perform risk assessment, mitigation, and change management throughout the program lifecycle
- Domestic and international travel (~25%) to ODM/CM and design partner sites
A day in the life
You start the day reviewing first-pass yield data from an overnight Pilot build at your ODM, isolating a test station driving a recurring failure. Mid-morning, you lead a DFx review with hardware design, pushing changes to improve testability before design freeze. In the afternoon, you drive an RCCA on a solder defect with the CM quality team and update the control plan. You end the day refining the capacity plan and line balance for the next build phase.
About the team
The Hardware Engineering S3 Storage platform team is a group of engineers and technical program managers directly responsible for launching Storage servers into the AWS fleet. Located in Denver, Seattle, and Cupertino, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM/CM partners to deliver next-generation Storage server infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end-to-end, from server conception through volume production and fleet-scale operations.
Basic qualifications: - Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Chemical, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline
- 6+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in NPI, process development, or production engineering within semiconductor, server/datacenter hardware, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing
- 3+ years of end-to-end NPI product delivery experience from concept through volume production
- Hands-on experience with SMT assembly processes/PCB fabrication, or industrial automation or robotics
- Strong data analysis skills using statistical tools (JMP, Minitab, Excel, Python) to drive data-driven decisions
- Experience driving quality and schedule execution at multinational JDM, ODM, CM, and supplier partners
Preferred qualifications: - Master's degree in Manufacturing, Chemical, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of relevant industry experience spanning semiconductor equipment, wafer fab operations, advanced packaging, or high-volume server/networking hardware manufacturing
- Experience with Storage server platform manufacturing
- Experience with PLC programming, industrial controls, and automated test equipment (ATE) in production; ability to troubleshoot PLC-controlled systems and robotic work cells
- Process tool ownership including process-of-record (POR), recipe management, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), and OEE tracking for tools such as reflow ovens, pick-and-place, or AOI/AXI
- Experience with DOE (Design of Experiments), MSA (Measurement System Analysis), GR&R studies, and process capability analysis in a production setting
- Track record of driving yield improvement, DFx, PFMEA, and cost optimization through automation and process engineering
