title: Sr. Product Manager - Finance/ Supply Chain Analytics & Data Engineering, Amazon Leo Finance Acceleration (ALFA)
description:
Join us in revolutionizing global connectivity by shaping the future of satellite internet infrastructure. As a Product Manager, Technical (PMT) on the Amazon Leo Finance Technology team, you will own the product roadmap for finance and supply chain analytics — designing how data flows from transactional systems (SAP S/4HANA and non-SAP) into the reporting, dashboarding, and self-service analytics layer that drives operational and financial decision-making.
This role sits at the intersection of finance domain expertise, data engineering, and product management. You do not need to be a deep SAP domain expertise. You need to understand how finance and supply chain processes generate data — from procurement through fulfillment, warehouse operations, production-manufacturing activities, from journal entries through financial close — and own the product strategy that turns that data into trusted, timely, and actionable insights for our user groups.
You will work across finance, accounting, tax, legal, compliance, supply chain, and engineering teams, translating complex process and data requirements into a clear product roadmap that meets information and analytics needs. You will navigate ambiguity, build consensus across cross-functional stakeholders, and deliver analytics through partnering with Tech teams capabilities that support Amazon's satellite connectivity mission.
Key job responsibilities
Finance & Supply Chain Process Understanding
- Develop deep understanding of end-to-end finance and accounting processes as it relates to — Procure-to-Pay, Management Accounting, Record-to-Report, and Production/ Manufacturing and Warehouse operations — and how each process generates, transforms, and consumes data across the enterprise.
- Understand supply chain data flows — demand planning, inventory, fulfillment, logistics, and procurement — and how they connect to financial reporting and cost analytics.
- Map data lineage from source ERP transactions (SAP S/4HANA and non-SAP systems) through integration layers into analytics platforms, identifying gaps, latency, and quality issues.
Product Management & Roadmap Ownership
- Own the end-to-end product roadmap for finance and supply chain analytics initiatives, including integration between transactional systems and the BI/analytics stack.
- Define and prioritize product features and requirements to ensure timely delivery of analytics capabilities that serve finance stakeholders.
- Drive product vision, goals, tenets, and monthly business reviews with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
- Develop use cases by gathering operating requirements, partner with engineering and data teams to build required features, communicate dependencies, and manage exceptions.
- Write clear business cases, solution narratives, and functional/technical documentation.
Data Engineering & BI
- Own the analytics and reporting product layer — designing dashboards, data pipelines, data models, and self-service analytics tools using AWS services (QuickSight, Athena, Redshift, Glue, S3) or equivalent.
- Define data quality, governance, and lineage standards for finance and supply chain data flowing into the analytics platform.
- Build and validate Proof of Concepts (POCs) to demonstrate that proposed analytics solutions meet business requirements.
- Participate in testing cycles (unit, integration, UAT), user training, deployment, and post-deployment support for analytics products.
Cross-Functional Leadership
- Navigate ambiguity and drive consensus across finance, engineering, supply chain, and compliance teams.
- Communicate project status clearly to technical and non-technical leadership and follow appropriate escalation channels.
- Champion agile delivery practices within the product development lifecycle.
A day in the life
Your morning might start with a data lineage review — tracing how cost center postings flow from SAP MES into your Redshift data warehouse and surfacing a latency issue that delays the weekly cost variance dashboard. Mid-morning, you lead a product review with finance leadership, walking through roadmap trade-offs between building a new self-service P&L drill-down in QuickSight versus automating the month-end accruals reconciliation report. After lunch, you work with your data engineering team to define acceptance criteria for a new supply chain procurement analytics pipeline, then close the day by drafting the business case for a forecasting feature that combines ERP actuals with demand planning signals.
You engage with diverse teams across time zones, translating complex financial and supply chain data flows into product decisions that accelerate insight and reduce manual reporting effort.
About the team
We are a pioneering group dedicated to expanding global internet access through satellite technology. Our team thrives on innovation, collaboration, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on digital inclusion worldwide. We are building something extraordinary that will transform how unconnected communities experience technology and communication.

title: Sr. Product Manager - Tech
description:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Product Manager, Power Conversion Systems HVDC to own the product strategy and roadmap for the HVDC Solid-State Transformer (SST) platform. The right person can understand and articulate data-center customer needs, grid-code constraints, and the competitive landscape, distill them into a clear, prioritized product definition, and drive the cross-functional execution that turns the engineering platform into a deployable, differentiated product.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
As a Product Manager, Power Conversion Systems HVCE you own the SST product, a greenfield, megawatt-class product with no reference design to lean on — the strategy, the roadmap, and the business case behind it. You own understanding and articulating data-center customer needs, grid-code constraints, and the competitive landscape, distilling them into a clear, prioritized product definition. You will make cross-domain trade-offs that reconcile competing demands into a single plan, and set direction across engineering and go-to-market execution that turns the engineering platform into a deployable, differentiated product. You will also communicate decisions and risks to specialists and leadership, keeping everyone aligned through steady, frequent communication as a core part of your role.
Key job responsibilities
SST platform ownership:
Own the strategy, the roadmap, and the business case behind the SST platform.
Define a multi-generation roadmap tied to where data center power is heading.
Communicate decisions and risks to leadership and partner teams.
SST product requirements:
Spend time understanding customers, the competitive landscape, and the grid-code realities that constrain what’s possible.
Define the prioritized list of product requirements.
Reconcile customer needs, engineering limits, cost targets, schedule, and grid requirements into a clear prioritized product definition.
SST product development:
Own driving product development from concept to launch.
Work with engineering and go-to-market partner teams through phase/gate and executive reviews.
Outline the serviceability and lifecycle plans associated with shipping hardware.
SST System Alignment:

Correlate thermal models with efficiency, load-profile and qualification data across the SST operating envelope.
A day in the life
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to celebrate our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and diversity conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We have a career path for you no matter what stage you’re in when you start here. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Sr. Product Manager – Technical, Amazon Leo
description:
Amazon Leo is building a constellation of 3,000+ Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband connectivity to customers around the world. The Leo Connectivity Product team is responsible for defining and delivering the end-to-end networking and service experiences that connect customers — consumers, enterprises, and the public sector — to the Leo network.
We are seeking a highly technical Sr. Product Manager to own product definition for future generations of Leo’s satellite connectivity system. This is a strategic, cross-functional role focused on identifying the customer problems we will solve with next-generation architectures. You will work at the intersection of vehicle engineering, software engineering, modeling and simulation, and the PMT teams building our first-generation network, constellation and customer devices — synthesizing insights across all of them to define what comes next.
This role requires someone who thrives in ambiguity. The problems are not yet well-defined, the solution space is wide open, and the timelines may be long. You will frame ill-defined challenges into actionable product strategies, drive system-level trade studies with modeling and simulation teams and translate technical possibilities into customer-centric product direction. This is a high-visibility individual contributor role based in Redmond, WA.
*** Export Control Requirement ***
- Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
- Define the product vision and requirements for future-generation satellite connectivity systems, grounded in deep understanding of customer problems across consumer, enterprise, and public sector segments.
- Drive system-level trade studies in partnership with modeling and simulation teams — translating simulation outputs into product requirements and investment recommendations.
- Partner deeply with vehicle engineering and software engineering to understand technical constraints and opportunities that inform future system architectures.
- Collaborate with PMTs owning first-generation constellation systems and customer antenna products to identify gaps, lessons learned, and opportunities that shape future generations.
- Frame ambiguous, long-horizon problems into structured product strategies with clear hypotheses, evaluation criteria, and decision frameworks.
- Write PRFAQs, technical narratives, and investment proposals that articulate the customer need, technical approach, and business case for future system capabilities.
- Represent the futures roadmap in leadership reviews, clearly communicating trade-offs, dependencies, and strategic rationale to senior technical and business stakeholders.
A day in the life
Your morning might begin with a review of simulation results from the modeling team — a new trade study has landed overnight comparing architectural approaches for a capability that could unlock performance improvements for enterprise customers. You dig into the data, identify the assumptions that need stress-testing, and draft follow-up questions for the simulation engineers.
Mid-morning, you’re in a working session with vehicle engineering, walking through how a proposed design change to the satellite bus impacts the connectivity services you’re defining. You push on the customer experience implications and propose a set of requirements that preserve flexibility for future service evolution.
After lunch, you sit down with a PMT colleague who owns our payload software. Together you review field data and customer feedback, looking for patterns that signal where the current architecture falls short and where the next generation needs to leap forward. You capture three hypotheses to validate with simulation runs.
The afternoon is heads-down writing time. You’re drafting a narrative that frames a customer problem — one that doesn’t have an obvious solution yet — and propose an evaluation framework for the engineering team to assess multiple architectural paths. You end the day in a cross-functional sync, aligning vehicle, software, and simulation teams on priorities for the next sprint of trade studies.
About the team
You’ll be part of the Leo Global Product team — a group of product and technology leaders responsible for defining the end-to-end connectivity experience for Leo’s customers. Our team spans device products, networking services, enterprise solutions, and future systems.
We value deep technical curiosity, comfort with ambiguity, and a relentless focus on the customer problems worth solving. We operate with a builder’s mentality — moving fast on the things we understand and moving deliberately on the things that require getting it right. We are a team that debates rigorously, decides clearly, and supports each other once a direction is set.
We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe the best products come from teams with varied perspectives and experiences.

- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Experience in aerospace, satellite communications, telecommunications systems, or a related field
Preferred qualifications: - Background in satellite communications, space systems, or LEO constellation architectures.
- Experience defining products that span multiple customer segments (consumer, enterprise, public sector).
- Experience working with large-scale simulation and modeling systems to inform product decisions and system architecture trade-offs.

title: Sr. Product Manager, Communities, SPC
description:
The Selling Partner Communities & Empowerment ("Communities") organization builds lasting connections with Amazon's Selling Partners (SPs) and helps them succeed. Our products, including Seller Forums, Seller News, and emerging community platforms, are used by millions of Selling Partners worldwide to engage with Amazon and with each other. These products also surface critical insights into SP sentiment and emerging issues. Our goal is to make every Selling Partner feel satisfied about selling in Amazon stores.
We are seeking a Sr. Product Manager who is passionate about the seller experience and about using generative AI to rethink how sellers connect, learn, and get help. The role sits where customer insight, business strategy, and AI innovation meet. You will use GenAI to experiment quickly, test new ideas, and launch experiences that weren't possible before. You will own the product vision, roadmap, and go-to-market for parts of our community product suite. You will turn seller needs and sentiment into clear product direction, drive adoption, and measure business impact. This is a high-ambiguity, high-impact role: you will shape one of Amazon's largest online seller communities, align a diverse set of stakeholders, and deliver results that improve how millions of sellers connect, learn, and succeed.
Key job responsibilities
Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for community products, from working backwards (PR/FAQ, tenets, problem statement) through launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration
Define product vision, strategy, and roadmap for seller-facing community experiences and the internal tools community managers and business teams use
Use generative AI tools to quickly prototype, test, and validate new community experiences, such as AI-assisted content, personalized seller journeys, and automated insights
Run fast experiments on new features and programs, learn quickly, and scale what works
Be the voice of the Selling Partner, using quantitative data (forums analytics, sentiment trends, engagement metrics) and qualitative research (user studies, focus groups, seller interviews), and separate representative signal from anecdotal feedback
Turn seller pain points and sentiment insights into clear business requirements, user stories, and prioritized product decisions
Own go-to-market for launches, including positioning, messaging, seller education, and adoption campaigns, in partnership with marketing, communications, and international teams
Reason from first principles: challenge assumptions, avoid defaulting to past approaches, and build solutions from the core customer need

description:
AWS Data Center Learning's mission is to develop the best data center workforce on Earth. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role at the intersection of workforce development, operational excellence, and technical rigor. You will serve as the program owner for a portfolio of certifications that directly influence the safety, quality, and reliability of AWS infrastructure worldwide.
Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the multi-year roadmap for technical certification programs across global AWS data center job families (DCO, DCEO, DCMAT)
- Develop and maintain a competency-based certification framework aligned to the AWS Data Center Builder Competency Framework, ensuring certifications serve as independent validators of real-world skill — not proxies for training completion
- Lead Job Task Analysis (JTA) and partner with others to translate broad competency standards into defensible, psychometrically sound certification assessments
- Partner in the design and development of certification assessments (written, practical, and performance-based) in partnership with subject matter experts, instructional designers, and third-party assessment vendors
- Ensure independence between training and certification development to maintain assessment integrity and prevent "teaching to the test"
- Establish and govern item development, review, and validation processes across global content contributors
- Drive end-to-end program delivery across multiple time zones, regions, and regulatory environments — from pilot launch through scaled global rollout
- Define and manage certification delivery infrastructure including LMS integrations, proctoring solutions, and credentialing platforms

- Influence without authority across training, operations, safety, HR, legal, and regional site leadership to align certification programs with business priorities

- Use data to identify gaps, prioritize investments, and drive continuous improvement across the certification portfolio
- Stay current on industry best practices in technical credentialing, psychometrics, and workforce capability frameworks
A day in the life
Your morning kicks off with a coffee in one hand and a certification pass rate dashboard in the other — because somewhere in EMEA, a pilot just wrapped and the data is interesting. You spot an anomaly suggesting training and assessment have quietly drifted apart, fire off a note to the JTA lead, and feel that particular satisfaction of catching something before it becomes someone else's problem. Mid-morning, you're on a call with a third-party vendor, diplomatically but firmly explaining why their proposed shortcut is a no-go — assessment integrity isn't negotiable. After lunch, you're turning a gnarly dependency map into a crisp two-pager for a VP business review, making the case for more resourcing to accelerate certification coverage in APAC. Late afternoon brings a working session with your instructional design partners and a site lead dialing in from Singapore, collectively figuring out whether a new performance-based assessment can scale across 12 sites with wildly different equipment setups (spoiler: it can). You close the day by unblocking a cross-functional team stuck on a credentialing platform integration — technically not your problem, until it is — and updating your roadmap before logging off. It's a lot. It's also kind of great.

The DC Certifications team is redefining how work readiness is measured across AWS data centers. Rather than tracking training completion, we deliver outcome-based certifications that validate whether a Builder can confidently do the job.
Our program assesses competencies tied to specific data center tasks, using practical and simulated environments to maintain high, consistent standards. We automate assessment delivery to keep the process simple, while ensuring independence and rigor through qualified assessors. Behind the scenes, we provide the tooling and data solutions that help sites plan and manage their workforce's capabilities.
Certifications are either role-based — mandatory for all Builders as part of onboarding and development — or specialty-based, tied to specific hardware or tools and managed by demand. title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Shipping Speed, Selection & Charges, Shipping Platform
description:
Every time someone shops on Amazon, our systems influence what they see about delivery: whether an item can ship to them, how fast it will arrive, and what shipping will cost. We own shipping speed, selection and charges for Amazon stores around the world. Our 6 Tier-1 services sit on the critical path of every product page, cart and checkout, handling millions of requests per second before checkout. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help us modernize how that works and to change how we build software along the way.
You'll lead three programs that matter to customers and to how we build:
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilities. Our ship options were first built just to describe speed. Over time each one also took on other delivery features, so a single identifier now does several jobs across many ordering, delivery and fulfillment systems. You'll drive the multi-year platform change that lets teams launch new delivery experiences, like ultra-fast quick commerce, age-verified delivery or grocery delivery, by combining reusable building blocks. Today each one needs a new ship option.
Build the customer rescue product. When an item can't be delivered to a customer, the purchase shouldn't end there. Our team is building customer rescue, the product that catches these dead ends across the shopping journey and help customers complete their order: healing carts and checkouts with substitutes and alternate offers and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery. You'll drive its delivery and adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce and other programs, partnering with the teams who own each experience.
Help lead our move to AI-driven software development. We're building toward a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in where human judgment matters. You'll own the plan to roll this out across our teams, decide how we measure success.
You'll work with principal engineers, product managers and engineering leaders across Amazon, and you'll regularly write for and present to senior leadership.
Key job responsibilities
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilites
Own the roadmap to move Amazon's ordering and delivery systems off ship-option-specific logic and onto reusable capabilities and signals, so new delivery experiences launch without new ship options.
Drive adoption across shipping, checkout, fulfillment and transportation systems. Sequence integrations, align designs with principal and senior engineers, and onboard new businesses such as quick commerce, grocery and age-verified delivery.
Customer rescue product
Drive delivery of the customer rescue product from roadmap to launch: cart and checkout healing with substitutes and alternate offers, clear restriction messages, and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery.
Lead adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce, partnering with the teams who own each shopping experience.
Coordinate A/B experiments, staged rollouts and launch readiness across marketplaces, and use the results to drive launch decisions.
Run weekly, monthly and business reviews with senior leadership, with written narratives on results, risks, recovery plans and decisions needed.
AI-driven software development
Own the plan to move our teams to a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in at key decision points. Push for full adoption over isolated pilots.
Define how adoption and impact are measured, such as coverage by service, changes shipped through agents and automated test coverage.
A day in the life
Your morning might start chairing the Ship Option Control Board, where you and principal engineers from several organizations decide whether a new delivery experience should be a reusable capability or a signal. Later you turn the latest customer rescue experiment readout into a clear recommendation for the weekly leadership review, then meet with a partner team to plan bringing the product into their shopping experience. In the afternoon you sit with a team moving its service to AI-driven development, find where the agents still get stuck, and fold those gaps into the adoption plan. You might end the day tuning an agent that drafts your program update from tracker data, so the next one takes minutes instead of hours.

title: AI Applied Scientist, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.
Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.
The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.
Strong proficiency in Python and the modern ML ecosystem, with demonstrated ability to implement complex methods from recent papers and run large-scale experiments.
Hands-on experience with large language models, whether fine-tuning, inference, prompting pipelines, or building LLM-powered applications.
Demonstrated research ability through publications at peer-reviewed venues, preprints, or equivalent research output.
Track record of applying research to practical problems: methods, prototypes, or tools adopted by other teams or used to inform real product decisions.
Solid software engineering fundamentals for research code: version control, testing, reproducibility, and code others can build on.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex results, and their limitations, to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and new problem spaces; you thrive when building something that doesn't yet have a playbook.
Preferred qualifications: First-author publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), especially on evaluation methodology: papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation to demonstrate model improvements.
Specific experience in one or more of: LLM-as-judge approaches (calibration, rubric design, bias mitigation); benchmark design and validation (IRT, contamination detection); human evaluation methodology (protocol design, quality control); experimentation and comparisons between system versions (A/B testing, uncertainty quantification); or agentic and multi-agent system evaluation, including failure diagnosis and automated red-teaming.
Familiarity with theoretical foundations of evaluation: measurement theory and validity frameworks, statistical learning theory (calibration, reliability, decision theory), causal inference, or preference aggregation.
Experience with the practical challenges of evaluating generative AI and agentic systems: non-deterministic outputs, token economics, multi-turn agent trajectories, and tool use.
Experience building methods or tools used directly by non-experts, such as developer-facing ML tooling or self-service analytics.
Familiarity with modern evaluation tools and frameworks (e.g., DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, LangSmith, or agent tracing and observability tools).
Experience working with distributed computing or cloud-native tooling (e.g., Ray, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes) to run evaluations at scale.
Experience with cross-disciplinary work, such as collaboration with social scientists, psychometricians, or domain experts.
Experience in fast-moving, early-stage teams where you helped define technical direction from the ground up.

title: Americas Logistics- Transportation Manager
description:

If you enjoy structuring complex systems, building tools that make work scale, and connecting RF hardware and software teams, this role is for you.
In this role, you will be responsible for the optimal interaction between our RF transceivers and RF front-end modules. You will turn advanced cellular capabilities, such as carrier aggregation, MIMO, SRS antenna switching and Multi-SIM into concrete transceiver and front-end configurations. You will work closely with transmitter and receiver teams to define and refine these configurations, and partner with hardware, software and validation teams to bring them into our products. You will develop tooling and automation that keep configurations consistent across programs and contribute to the system design documentation that guides implementation.
Minimum qualifications: Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree
Solid understanding of 3GPP 5G NR and LTE physical layer and RF requirements, including band combinations, carrier aggregation, MIMO and SRS.
Working knowledge of RF front-end architectures and the system-level impact of components like PAs, LNAs, filters, and switches.
Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or C/C++ for data analysis, system modeling, and algorithm development.
Ability to critically analyze complex trade-offs, such as routing flexibility versus insertion loss or throughput versus battery life.
Strong communication skills with a proven ability to work across diverse, cross-functional teams to solve highly complex, multi-disciplinary problems.

5+ years of experience in RF systems engineering or 10+ years in communications circuit design.
Experience translating system requirements into hardware configurations, control settings or structured system descriptions.
Familiarity with RF configuration frameworks is a plus.
Enjoy structuring complex information with a strong focus on precision and consistency.
Experience applying AI/ML to solve system-level optimization problems.
History of successfully balancing cutting-edge hardware innovation with the practical constraints of high-volume manufacturing.

title: Commercial & Strategy Manager (CSM) Supply Chain - Mechanical Enclosures
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.

Excellent communicators, capable of working in multinational environments, driven and motivated by accomplishing extraordinary objectives
Mechanical and/or prior technical acumen to effectively negotiate by leveraging manufacturing process and product design fundamentals

title: Custom Circuit RTL Design Engineer
description:
Do you love creating elegant solutions to highly complex challenges? Do you intrinsically see the importance in every detail? As part of our Silicon Technologies group, you’ll help design and manufacture our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient processor, system-on-chip (SoC). You’ll ensure Apple products and services can seamlessly and efficiently handle the tasks that make them beloved by millions. Joining this group means you’ll be responsible for crafting and building the technology that fuels Apple’s devices. Together, you and your team will enable our customers to do all the things they love with their devices. Do you have a passion for crafting entirely new solutions?
As part of our Digital Circuits Group, youʼll take imaginative and revolutionary ideas and determine how to turn them into reality! You and your team will apply engineering fundamentals and start from scratch if needed, bringing forward-thinking ideas to the real world! Your efforts will be groundbreaking, often literally. Join us, and youʼll help design the tools that allow us to bring customers experiences they have never-before envisioned. You will be part of an exciting silicon design group that is responsible for designing pioneering ASICs. In this role as a Custom Circuit RTL Design Engineer, you will be working with the custom circuits team to implement behavioral and structural RTL models of advanced custom digital circuits, translate specifications in assertions models, and verify equivalence of the RTL models to circuits. You will be at the heart of a processor design effort, making a critical impact delivering products to market quickly.
In this highly visible role as a Custom Circuits RTL Design Engineer, you will be at the center of a SoC design effort collaborating with all teams, with a critical impact on getting bug-free functional products to market quickly. This requires you to work closely with the circuit design team to review design and architecture specifications and with various design teams across the SoC partitions to understand the use cases and corner conditions to develop test plans. Furthermore, you will be required to develop the methodology for test benches and coverage monitors for functional coverage and assertions. You will also work on improving the RTL methodology as applicable to simulation and emulation scenarios.
You will have the responsibilities as follows:
- Design and implement behavioral RTL models for various custom SRAM arrays.
- Work with logic/architecture team to determine specifications and assertions for custom SRAM arrays.
- Work closely with custom circuit team to review schematics and understand how the RTL must model it.
- Work closely with DV teams to verify functionality.
- Work with SOC teams to successfully integrate custom RTL design into chip.
- Implement RTL methodology and new flows with understanding of GenAI capabilities and limitations in hardware design to successfully integrate custom RTL design into chip.
- Use GenAI assisted tools for faster debug and turnaround time.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years of relevant industry experience
Preferred qualifications: In-depth knowledge of digital design, behavioral (including emulation-friendly) and structural RTL coding especially as it pertains to SRAM and register file design
Knowledge of Verilog, System Verilog and experience with industry standard simulators and waveform debugging tools
Knowledge of regression and revision control tools, and scripting language (python / perl)
Knowledge of industry standard design and verification tools, such as ESPCV and/or LEC
Knowledge of regression and revision control tools.
Basic knowledge of viewing and understanding custom circuit schematics
Knowledge of custom circuit and SRAM design and DFT (ATPG/MBIST) is desirable.

title: Design Ops - Integrated Producer
description:
Apple TV's Marketing team crafts world-class campaigns that connect audiences with high-quality stories — building brand awareness and loyalty. We drive innovation and excellence — from strategic vision to creative execution — collaborating across the Apple ecosystem, as well as agencies, studios, and talent to place Apple TV at the heart of global culture.
The Operations team within Apple TV Marketing is tasked with building processes/workflows, managing budgets, and facilitating all creative production in partnership with our creative teams. Within Operations, the Integrated Producer works in lockstep with our Creative Directors, Art Directors and Strategists, as well as a multitude of cross-functional partners and external agencies, ensuring all key art, OOH, digital, and social assets are produced and delivered across a variety of multi-channel paid, owned, and earned channels -- all in support of Apple TV original series, films, brand, and most recently, sports. In short, they keep the trains running on time and on budget, while ensuring all static creative goes from a PDF in an email to a pristine billboard on Sunset. While the Creative and Strategy leads are establishing the “what” and the “why” of our campaign assets & strategy, the Operations team — more specifically, the Producers — are driving the “how.”

* Serve as the source of truth & central hub for all creative status information, updating tools, decks, and documents with dates, schedules, and next steps — ensuring all internal parties are informed as the overall status evolves by the day (or even minute).

title: Embedded Software Engineer - Always On Platforms, Core OS
description:
Every time your iPhone detects a car crash and calls for help, your Apple Watch notices you’ve started a workout before you tell it to, or “Hey Siri” wakes up without you touching a thing, there’s a tiny, always-on processor making it happen. At Apple, the Always-On Processor (AOP) firmware team builds the software that runs on that silicon. We write the firmware that listens to the world through accelerometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers, and more, while sipping just microwatts of power.
Our work sits underneath features people rely on every day, from emergency response and fitness tracking to camera image stabilization, spatial audio, intuitive device interactions, and all-day battery life. Because the same platform spans iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, Mac, AirPods, and Vision Pro, a line of code you write can ship in products used by hundreds of millions of people. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something!
The Core Operating Systems (Core OS) team is responsible for the foundational software used in Apple’s most iconic and beloved products. We’re looking for a talented Embedded Software Engineer to join the Always On Platform Systems team. This team is uniquely positioned to contribute to all Apple products and has a wide range of responsibilities including: pre-silicon software development, hardware bringup, sensor driver development and integration, as well as future framework and feature development for the Always On technology area. The team also has oversight responsibilities in architecture, compute and memory resourcing, and cross-functional feature deployment.
The ideal candidate must possess a genuine passion for hardware/software integration, software quality, and the ability to collaborate and communicate effectively across teams. This is a rare opportunity to help build cutting-edge foundational technologies and have a direct impact on Apple’s widely loved products across the globe.
Minimum qualifications: Proven experience in embedded software development.
Strong proficiency in C/C++ programming.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
BS degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent skills/experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with real-time operating systems (RTOS).
Familiarity with hardware architectures (ARM preferred).
Solid Hardware and Software debugging skills.
Understanding of common peripheral busses (SPI/I2C/USB)
Experience with sensor integration.
Knowledge of Apple platforms and technologies.

title: Principal Security Architect, Data Center Security
description:
The Apple Services Engineering Security team is looking for a principal-level security architect to own end-to-end trust for Apple’s next generation of data center infrastructure, the assurance that every physical and logical component, from silicon to the running workload, operates in a known, verifiable, tamper-evident state, and that this trust can be cryptographically proven to any relying party before access or data is granted. This spans hardware root of trust, DPU/IPU offload security, software and workload integrity, and the attestation protocols that tie them together into a single verifiable chain. You will partner with silicon, firmware, SOC architecture, platform, and cloud infrastructure teams to design and integrate this stack, and you’ll represent Apple in the standards bodies that define how this trust travels across the industry.
You will architect and integrate security across four layers of the data center stack:
Hardware root of trust — secure boot chains anchored in silicon (fuses, eFuse-based identity, HSMs), platform firmware integrity (UEFI/BIOS measured boot), and the physical/supply-chain controls that establish an immutable, device-unique identity at power-on.
IPU/DPU and offload security — working with platform and networking teams to ensure SmartNICs/DPUs/IPUs, as the emerging trust boundary isolating tenant workloads from infrastructure management, have their own attestable root of trust, not just line-rate crypto and policy enforcement.
Software and workload integrity — measured, signed boot through hypervisor/OS/container runtime with an unbroken chain of custody from firmware to running workload; confidential computing primitives (enclaves, TEEs, confidential VMs); drift detection against measured baselines.
Attestation and verifiable trust — the mechanism that converts the above into a dynamic, per-session trust decision: signed quotes of measured state, verification against golden measurements, key sealing/unsealing tied to attestation results, revocation of compromised measurements, and remote attestation protocols that let this trust travel to the relying party that needs it, including the agent identity layer sitting on top of this stack.
You will drive design reviews and threat models with SOC architects and platform teams, define the architecture that lets each layer attest up to the next, and ensure quality and agility through rigorous testing, participating in on-call for the systems you ship.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of security/software engineering experience, including systems-level and infrastructure security
Deep, hands-on experience with hardware root-of-trust architectures (TPM, DICE, or equivalent) and measured/attested boot chains
Proven track record designing or implementing remote attestation protocols, key sealing/provisioning tied to attestation state, and measurement revocation
Proficiency in at least one of C, C++, Go, Rust, or Python, with solid Linux systems fundamentals
Experience designing gRPC/REST backend services for identity, key management, or attestation at scale
Preferred qualifications: Direct experience with DPU/IPU/SmartNIC security architectures — tenant isolation from infrastructure management, line-rate crypto offload, and attestable DPU firmware/identity
Contribution to industry standards for root of trust or attestation (TCG, OCP, Caliptra, DMTF/SPDM, Redfish)

As an engineering manager in SPEAR, you will lead projects in collaboration with the maintainers of core operating system components to harden the security of our operating systems. Your team will deliver well-designed, robust, and maintainable system software features that meaningfully improve end-user security. The team will be on the leading edge of responsible AI adoption, unlocking new possibilities to achieve ambitious security goals with higher quality than was previously attainable. As a leader in a growing organization, you will hire and develop talented engineers who will help set the standard for cross-functional collaboration and engineering excellence.
As a result of the collective effort of dedicated engineers like yourself, Apple's products are the most secure consumer devices on the market. Our mission is to continue to advance the state of the art in software security. Our goal isn't simply to be the most secure: we're working to ensure the safety of every user's digital life, even against the most malicious and well-resourced adversaries.

Hands-on experience with software development in a system language such as Swift, Rust, Objective-C, or C++

title: Senior Camera Imaging Software Engineer - Camera & Photos
description:
iPhone is the most popular camera in the world, with billions of photos taken every year. The seamless integration of software and hardware has led to camera features like the Photonic Engine, Portrait mode, and Super-high-resolution photos which deliver magical experiences that surprise and delight our customers.
The Camera Technologies & Systems team in the Camera & Photos org delivers amazing quality photos and videos by combining state of the art computer vision, image processing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Familiarity with machine learning acceleration on the ANE or comparable hardware.

Strong programming skills, especially in Objective-C or C++

title: Senior Data Engineer - Business & Education
description:

title: Senior Engineering Manager - Apple Cloud Storage Infrastructure
description:

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI - Proactive
description:

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Conversational AI - Services Special Projects
description:

We're building a massive, real-time conversational experience from the ground up, one that will reach users at Apple scale. It sits at the intersection of Generative AI, Information Retrieval, and Knowledge Graphs.
We're looking for a senior machine learning engineer to own the conversational intelligence layer: the agent's reasoning and tool-calling, the low-latency LLM inference behind it, and the knowledge services that keep every response accurate and grounded. You'll work closely with AI/ML scientists and engineers across the stack. title: Senior Research Manager, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function. It is a foundational science. As these systems grow in complexity, the quality of our products is increasingly constrained by the quality of our evaluation methods. Our team is building the scientific foundation and self-service tools for how AI evaluation is done at scale, spanning LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship. We don’t just publish methods; we productionize them. We are looking for a Sr. Research Manager to lead an interdisciplinary research team that advances the state-of-the-art in evaluation methods that can be shipped as production tools for Apple developers and published in top venues.
We are looking for a Sr. Research Manager to lead an interdisciplinary research team advancing the frontier of evaluation methods. The team works in close collaboration with applied scientists and measurement scientists to build evaluation methodology and systems that are human-centered, psychometrically rigorous, and technically frontier. You will set the research agenda, direct the team's portfolio across near-term and long-term bets, and ensure that novel methods are designed from the outset for productionization into evaluation SDKs and APIs. You will have a strong background in ML or a closely related quantitative field and a track record of leading research teams that publish at top venues while simultaneously shipping methods into production tools.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will lead ML researchers, measurement scientists, and applied scientists, bringing together frontier ML research, psychometric and statistical rigor, and production engineering. What unites the strongest candidates is depth of thinking about evaluation as a research problem and the conviction that how we measure AI systems is as important as how we build them.

5+ years of experience managing or leading research teams in an industry setting, with demonstrated ability to attract and retain strong research talent
Experience publishing research at top-tier AI/ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP) or comparable venues in statistics or measurement
Experience partnering with applied science and engineering teams to translate research into production systems, tools, or capabilities adopted by others
Technical depth in AI evaluation, with the ability to critically assess and advance methods for measuring AI system behavior, whether through automated judgment, benchmark design, synthetic data, human evaluation, experimentation, failure analysis, or other approaches

Excellent communication skills, including the ability to represent research to executive leadership, partner teams, and the external research community

Publications or demonstrated expertise specifically in evaluation methodology (papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation)

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Ads

Apple is where we use the power of technology to enrich people's lives. title: Software Developement Manager, Apple Services Engineering
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).

title: UX Designer
description:
At Beats, a passion for music brings diverse minds together to deliver innovative audio and accessory experiences for our customers. Our team conceptualizes, designs, and ships the user experience for Beats products, driving hardware and software innovation through Apple's seamless integration of design and engineering. Through deep collaboration, we make each other’s ideas stronger to create something wonderful to share with the world. The Beats Human Interface design team is looking for a designer whose ideas will impact the interaction, graphic, sound, and haptic experiences used by millions worldwide. As a problem solver and self-starter working in a fast-paced environment, you bring a unique blend of interaction, visual, and prototyping skills. You will collaborate with design and engineering partners to execute end-user experiences, while using storytelling and visuals to influence new, innovative concepts. Apply today!
In this role, you will take creative and technical ownership of complete projects, and transform complex challenges into seamless, user-centered designs. As a go-to expert and innovator within the team, you will shape intuitive interaction concepts, collaborate and align cross-functional partners, and create experiences that shape the Beats product landscape.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree in UX Design, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) or a related field
You have a solid portfolio demonstrating your design thinking, hands-on expertise, and problem-solving skills, and you can confidently speak to your work
You clearly communicate complex concepts and designs through sketches, wireframes, high-fidelity comps, and prototypes
You are highly proficient in industry-standard tools you need to visualize your ideas and deliver the work (such as Sketch, Adobe Creative Suite, Keynote)
You are comfortable with working independently and cross-functionally in a multi-disciplinary design and technical environment
You possess exceptional problem-solving skills, keen attention to detail, and the adaptability to pivot quickly to new inputs or priorities
You excel in written and verbal communication, and can present and defend your work effectively to large groups and leadership
Preferred qualifications: Previous experience working within Beats UX Design
Demonstrated ability to design complete sensory experiences that seamlessly blend digital interfaces with physical hardware
Expertise in handling simultaneous complex projects while maintaining high quality design standards—excels in time management
Track record of project leadership and creative thinking to influence product features
High level of curiosity for technology amplified by your design craft
Proven commitment to designing inclusive and accessible products
Knowledge of and experience with advanced prototyping in interaction tools and/or code

title: Vision Display, Optical Module Engineer
description:
Do something different! Apple is seeking a creative and dedicated Optical Module Engineer to contribute to the definition and delivery of innovative optical technologies for Apple’s next-generation vision display products. A successful candidate will possess exceptional technical skills and strong communication and leadership abilities to collaborate effectively with various Apple internal cross-functional teams and external suppliers.
In this role, you will be instrumental in defining critical optical module performance and integration requirements, developing key display features, and implementing effective testing and calibration strategies. Additionally, you will support the module development process from prototype to mass production.
This position provides you with a unique opportunity to translate key product requirements into hardware and features essential for delivering exceptional optical solutions and experiences across Apple’s next-generation products.
Define optical module and feature requirements, including prototype and validation strategies for future Apple vision display products.
Leverage lab equipment to demonstrate display user experience and tradeoffs to key decision makers
Develop integrated simulations and budgets to allocate key user experience figures of merit across multiple component requirements
Support daily activities related to build execution, module setup, data analysis, module failure analysis, and system integration.
Facilitate technical discussions with vendors and internal cross-functional teams.
Collaborate to establish optical module test and calibration requirements.
Foster innovation and introduce new technologies to enhance Apple’s vision display performance and user experience.
Utilize early hardware prototypes to propose solutions and conduct comprehensive trade-off analysis.
Effectively communicate the advantages, disadvantages, and risks to the broader team.
Minimum qualifications: B.S., M.S. or Ph.D. in Optics, EE, Physics, or a related field
4+ years of experience in the relevant industry
Experience in one or more of the following areas: optical design or architecture definition for augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR); display module requirement definition, design, and integration; display/system architecture; optical characterization; numerical modeling; image/video processing and machine learning; human and visual perception; and psychophysical studies.
Preferred qualifications: Experience in one or more of the following areas: development of optical module architectures from concept phase to MP; display technologies (e.g. µOLED, µLED); vendor management and multi-functional collaboration; optical simulation (ZEMAX, LightTools); software/algorithm development, programming (Python, Matlab); display pipeline optimization.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication and leadership abilities.

title: Wireless Bluetooth QA Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:
As a Bluetooth Quality Engineer, you will own the quality of Bluetooth-enabled features across Apple's product lineup — driving testing, validation, and engineering partnerships to deliver experiences customers love.
Join our Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems team and drive innovation that shapes how people experience technology every day. The Bluetooth Quality team is looking for a highly technical, motivated engineer who thrives on solving complex problems and brings strong collaborative skills to every challenge. In this role, you will ensure the quality and reliability of Bluetooth features across Apple's latest products, directly impacting the experience of millions of customers worldwide.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
1+ years of hands-on experience validating and testing products, with domain expertise in one or more of the following: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, NFC, Audio, or Networking
2+ years of experience defining test plans and creating test cases based on technical specifications and feature requirements
1+ years of experience developing test automation scripts using Python, Perl, or similar programming languages
Preferred qualifications: Proficiency in C++, C, Objective-C, or Swift
Obsessively passionate and inquisitive with a drive to solve everyday problems in innovative ways
Exceptional problem-solving, debugging, and critical thinking skills
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and documentation skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple teams and projects
Laser-focused on the smallest details that are most meaningful to customers
Strong time management skills with the ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
Experience with Continuous Integration tools such as Jenkins
Experience with AI tools and workflows is a plus

title: Wireless MAC Design Engineer
description:
Come join Apple’s wireless silicon development effort, with its emphasis on highly energy-efficient design and new technologies that transform the user experience at the product level, all of which is driven by a world-class vertically coordinated engineering team!
Develop MAC layer design for wireless communication SoCs, including creating microarchitecture and other documents based on system-level requirements, and writing area- and power-efficient RTL that is scalable. Work with systems and software teams to ensure performance and power efficiency. Collaborate with verification and emulation teams on debug, test plan review and code coverage closure. Run tools to ensure lint and CDC/RDC clean design. Work with synthesis team to review constraints, close timing and review area/timing reports.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, and 10+ years of relevant industry experience.
Digital logic design fundamentals.
Demonstrated experience in translating functional requirements into synthesizable Verilog or SystemVerilog RTL.
Knowledge of digital design flows such as RTL simulation and debug, synthesis, lint, STA, and LEC.
Ability to design multi-clock-domain logic and resolve CDC problems.
Preferred qualifications: 10+ years of experience in ASIC microarchitecture and RTL design.
Excellent organization skills.
Excellent communication skills – both written and oral.
Understanding wireless standards, such as IEEE 802.11, 802.15, Bluetooth or 3GPP.
Understanding of ASIC low power design techniques, e.g. multiple supply domains configuration and management, dynamic power/clock scaling and power analysis is a plus.

title: Wireless RF OTA MIMO Systems Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Do you like changing the game? As a Wireless RF OTA MIMO Systems Engineer, you will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of Apple’s customers every day. Apple's Wireless Systems team is looking for an engineer to develop the test systems and methodologies that characterize over-the-air performance across different wireless technologies for Apple's wireless products.
In this role, you will own the methodology behind our radiated MIMO measurements. You will design and verify OTA test systems that reproduce real-world propagation environments in the lab, develop test strategies for new wireless features as they come to market, and turn measurement data into clear insights about device performance. You will partner closely with cross-functional teams to find and resolve system-level issues early in the product cycle, and your work will directly influence design decisions across Apple’s wireless products.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in EE or equivalent with 10+ years of relevant work experience.
Strong technical background in wireless communication, including wireless protocols, antennas, and radio propagation.
Working experience with MIMO characteristics (at a system level), antenna design and requirements for modern wireless communication systems such as LTE, 5G NR (FR1/FR2) and Wi-Fi.
Strong problem solving and analytical skills.
Strong programming skills (MATLAB/Python).
Preferred qualifications: Master’s Degree in EE or equivalent with 10+ years of relevant work experience.
Working experience with different lab equipment: network analyzers, signal generators, signal analyzers, call boxes, channel emulators.
Experience with OTA test systems such as multi-probe anechoic chambers (MPAC), radiated two-stage (RTS), or reverberation chambers.
Familiarity with regulatory requirements and certification process for CTIA and 3GPP, including MIMO OTA test methodologies.
Experience with post-processing techniques and algorithms for extracting MIMO channel characterization metrics and other key performance indicators.
Knowledge of spatial channel models and their implementation in channel emulators.
Experience building test automation and data analysis pipelines.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work across hardware, software, and program teams.

title: Wireless RF OTA MIMO Validation Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Do you like changing the game? As a Wireless RF OTA MIMO Validation Engineer, you will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of Apple’s customers every day. Apple's Wireless Systems team is looking for an engineer to validate and certify the over-the-air performance of Apple's wireless products, from early prototypes through carrier and industry certification.
In this role, you will own MIMO OTA validation for Apple's wireless products from early prototypes through final certification. You will translate carrier, industry, and regulatory requirements into test cases, execute and maintain validation on our in-house OTA systems, and lead certification testing at third-party labs. You will drive debug across cross-functional teams and push for the design changes needed to get products ready to ship.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in EE or equivalent.
Hands-on experience with MIMO characteristics (at a system level), antenna design and requirements for modern wireless communication systems such as LTE, 5G NR (FR1/FR2).
Strong technical background in wireless communication.
Strong problem solving and analytical skills.
Strong programming skills (Matlab/Python).
Preferred qualifications: Master’s Degree in EE or equivalent.
Working experience with wireless protocols, antennas, and radio propagation.
Working experience with different lab equipment: network analyzers, signal generators, signal analyzers, call boxes, channel emulators.
Familiarity with regulatory requirements and certification process for CTIA and 3GPP, and PTCRB.
Experience running OTA measurements in anechoic chambers, including system calibration and measurement uncertainty.
Experience with test automation and scripting for lab equipment control and data analysis.
Strong organization and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple programs and deadlines.

title: Wireless System Design Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.
The people here at Apple don’t just build products — they craft the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
Our manufacturing wireless footprint grew 200% between 2024 and 2026, and we forecast
another 50% growth each year. Every new deployment adds clients, access points, and tighter
latency budgets to factory RF environments that are already crowded.
We are hiring a Wireless System Design Engineer to architect, secure, and debug these networks
at scale. You will own end-to-end wireless design on the factory floor:
• Spectrum and channel planning for dense deployments
• Low-latency design for time-critical test traffic
• Secure onboarding of thousands of device
When something breaks, you will lead root-cause analysis across client, AP, controller, and host
logs. You will also build the AI-driven analysis that makes this correlation fast, repeatable, and
increasingly automatic. You will partner with local operations, test, and network teams during new production line launches, so issues are resolved before they block production.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience in wireless and RF engineering, including hands-on design and
deployment on at least one enterprise Wi-Fi platform (e.g., HPE Aruba, Cisco
Catalyst/Meraki, Juniper Mist, Extreme, Ruckus).
Working knowledge of network access security and device identity: certificate-based
authentication, RADIUS, PKI, and zero-touch provisioning.
Wireless system design experience: spectrum and channel allocation in dense networks,
RF planning and site surveys, quality-of-service design, and low-latency tuning.
Solid networking fundamentals, including IP addressing and services, VLANs, and
routing.
Demonstrated use of AI to automate debugging, such as LLM- or ML-based workflows
that correlate logs, detect anomalies, or propose root causes, with results you can
describe and measure.
Python and Bash development skills: building and maintaining tools others rely on, with
version control, code review, and testing.
Preferred qualifications: Wireless deployments in manufacturing, industrial IoT, or other high-density, mission-
critical environments.
Familiarity with RF simulation and predictive planning tools, network security policy and
segmentation for device fleets, and Bluetooth or other short-range wireless coexistence
with Wi-Fi.
Industry certifications such as CWNE, CWNA, CWDP, CWAP, or vendor equivalents
(ACMX, CCNP Wireless)

title: Xcode Source Editor Engineer
description:
We're looking for an engineer to help build the Xcode IDE, a cornerstone of the Apple Developer Ecosystem. Millions of application developers use Xcode to deliver on their ambitions, and countless organizations use Xcode to transform ideas into launched applications.

description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Maintenance Planner to keep our facilities and production line equipment running. You'll plan preventive maintenance, schedule repairs, track parts, and make sure the right technician has the right job at the right time. This role resides within the maintenance/facilities team — if a line goes down, or output stops, your planning is what keeps things moving.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and maintain preventive maintenance schedules for facilities systems (HVAC, electrical, building infrastructure) and production line equipment

 - Turn maintenance requests into work orders — prioritize by urgency, safety, and impact on production

 - Track parts and spares inventory for production equipment, and order what's needed before it runs out

 - Coordinate with technicians, vendors, and outside contractors to schedule work around production schedules with minimal downtime

 - Maintain accurate records in the CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) work orders, asset history, downtime

 - Track maintenance costs and flag equipment that's costing more to fix than replace

 - Run weekly planning meetings with maintenance and production leads to review backlog and upcoming work




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 3+ years in maintenance planning or scheduling, ideally in a manufacturing or production environment

 - Experience with a CMMS (MaintainX, Maximo, SAP, or similar)

 - Comfortable reading equipment manuals and basic mechanical/electrical schematics

 - Strong organizational skills; juggling many work orders and know which one matters most today

 - Clear communicator; you'll be the point of contact between technicians, vendors, and production leaders

 - Equipment spare parts BOM experience

 - Spare parts crib management knowledge




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Facilities and Maintenance team is responsible for keeping Base Factory 1 running safely, reliably, and efficiently every hour of every shift. As Base scales production of home battery systems, this team builds the maintenance programs, reliability systems, and facility infrastructure that prevent downtime before it happens and enable manufacturing to meet growing customer demand. You'll have the opportunity to establish the foundation for a world-class maintenance organization—from preventive maintenance and spare parts strategy to equipment reliability and facility operations—rather than inheriting legacy systems. If you're excited by the challenge of building systems from the ground up, solving complex operational problems, and seeing the direct impact of your work on production output, quality, and company growth, this is a rare opportunity to shape the future of a rapidly scaling factory.
