title: Kitchen Manager, DashMart
description:
About the Team
We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 2+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.
You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness.
You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow.
You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small.
You’re a creative problem solver who challenges “how it’s always been done” and finds better ways forward.
You’re analytical, data-driven, and comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to make decisions.
As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
You’re comfortable flexing between kitchen and fulfillment operations, and you understand how culinary execution and order flow connect to overall site metrics like accuracy, quality, and efficiency.
You have (or can quickly learn) a working knowledge of inventory management systems (IMS), product flow, and fulfillment best practices within a multi-operation site.

About the Team
The Market Optimization team builds decision systems that help DoorDash invest in Dasher supply where it creates the greatest marketplace value. Market Optimizer brings together supply forecasts, causal response models, and constrained optimization to inform spending across acquisition, pay, and incentives. We work with the teams that own these levers to improve delivery speed and reliability while managing cost and supporting a healthy Dasher marketplace.
About the Role
We are looking for a hands-on technical leader to advance the causal models and production systems behind Mobilization. You will help answer where and when to offer incentives, how much to offer, and how long they should run. You will estimate the additional supply these decisions create and translate those estimates into dependable policies with Engineering, Product, Analytics, and Operations.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will
Build and calibrate response curves that estimate how incentive amount, timing, duration, and location affect incremental Dasher hours and marketplace outcomes.
Connect causal estimates and supply forecasts to constrained optimization, balancing delivery outcomes, incentive cost, and uncertainty across markets and time periods.
Design learning experiments and evaluation plans with Analytics. Account for marketplace spillovers, supply shifting between nearby areas or time periods, and interactions with other incentives.
Develop policies that direct spending toward periods when additional supply creates the most marketplace value, accounting for diminishing returns and non-linear delivery outcomes.
Own models through production deployment, calibration, monitoring, and incident diagnosis. Build diagnostics that explain policy changes and surface model or data regressions.

5+ years of experience developing causal inference or causal ML systems, with a record of using the results to change production decisions.
A record of leading ambiguous projects across team boundaries, making technical tradeoffs explicit, and developing other engineers.
Strong statistical judgment about randomized experiments and observational estimation, including confounding, treatment overlap, uncertainty, and the limits of causal claims.
Experience with treatment effect estimation or dose-response modeling and relevant methods such as doubly robust estimation, double machine learning, or off-policy evaluation. You choose methods based on the decision and available evidence.
Strong software and ML engineering skills. You can build reliable data and training pipelines, write maintainable production code, and diagnose failures across models and services.
Experience connecting models to constrained optimization, pricing, or resource allocation, and assessing how estimation errors affect production decisions.
The ability to explain modeling assumptions and incentive recommendations to partners who need to act on them.

About Compass
Compass is a new venture incubated within MISUMI Americas. We’re building it with the deep manufacturing expertise of Fictiv, MISUMI’s digital manufacturing platform.
Every physical product starts as a CAD model, and most of what it will cost is decided right there. Yet cost and manufacturability are still checked after the drawings are released, by hand and in spreadsheets, when every change is slow and expensive. The result is redesigns, missed schedules, and money left on the factory floor. Compass fixes that at the source. An engineer uploads an assembly, and Compass reads every part the way an expert manufacturing engineer would. It checks each feature against the processes that could make it, prices the part at the volume that matters, reads tolerances and GD&T straight off the drawing, and ranks exactly what to change. It does this across the entire bill of materials, reruns on every revision, and learns from every correction engineers make.
The problems underneath are genuinely hard: making sense of real-world geometry, modeling cost across machining, casting, molding, sheet metal, and additive, interpreting engineering drawings, and building AI that gets measurably better from expert feedback. The stakes are real, too. Our customers are enterprise engineering teams, including aerospace and defense programs, where the platform has to be as secure and trustworthy as it is smart. Compass is a small team that moves fast and gives engineers real ownership. You won’t inherit a finished system. You’ll help define the architecture, the security foundation, and the product that the most demanding customers in manufacturing will rely on.
About the Role
We’re looking for a cross-functional software engineer who thrives at the intersection of application development and cloud infrastructure. We’re scaling the product, fast-tracking SOC 2 Type I and Type II, and building an ITAR-ready environment for aerospace and defense customers. You’ll be one of the engineers who makes all three happen.
We don’t need a pure DevOps specialist managing servers all day. We need an engineer who treats infrastructure as code, automates our cloud environment to satisfy security audits, and writes clean application code to ship features customers use.
You’ll own our AWS infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines. In your first months, much of your time will go to building our compliance foundation. Over time, the role settles into roughly 30% platform automation and 70% full-stack feature development.

Accelerate SOC 2 compliance. Work with leadership to implement, automate, and maintain the AWS security controls SOC 2 requires: encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege IAM, logging, and vulnerability scanning.
Build our ITAR environment. Help design and run an isolated AWS GovCloud environment for customers with export-controlled data, with access restricted to US persons.
Own the platform. Manage, monitor, and scale our AWS environment using infrastructure as code (Terraform, AWS CDK, or Pulumi), with no manual configuration drift.
Build across the stack. Design, write, and deploy maintainable backend APIs and frontend features for our core product.
Automate everything. Maintain CI/CD pipelines (such as GitHub Actions) with automated testing, dependency scanning, and secure deployments built in.
Keep the architecture lean. Favor managed AWS services so the infrastructure needs minimal babysitting and you can focus on product.

location: New York City, New York, United States

Position Overview
The Senior Regional Air Freight Manager owns and leads all aspects of air freight performance, strategy, and business growth across assigned trade lanes and geographic territories (e.g., SouthCentral, Mountain and SouthWest/SoCal or designated regional trade lanes). This multi-dimensional role carries end-to-end financial accountability, down to Contribution Profit, while leading regional capacity procurement, bespoke door-to-door solution design, and go-to-market (GTM) commercial execution.
Serving as a key pillar of regional leadership, this role bridges global air freight strategy with local operational execution. You will act as a collaborative partner across cross-functional organizations (including Sales, Account Management, Global Procurement, Operations, Tech, and Finance) to expand market share, build strategic airline partnerships, and ensure flawless customer experience.
Key Responsibilities
1. Strategic Leadership & P&L Ownership
Strategic Planning & Target Setting: Define and execute the region’s long-term air freight vision, program initiatives, focus lanes, and growth objectives in close alignment with Global Air strategy and regional leadership (GM).
P&L & Financial Accountability: Own full financial performance (including Tonnage/Volume, Net Revenue, and Contribution Profit, e.g. Net Revenue minus Direct Costs ) for assigned regional origin/destination combinations and trade lanes.
Performance Governance & Metrics: Co-define annual budgets with General Management and actively participate in weekly business reviews (WBRs) to report on key metrics, yield performance, target adherence, and shortfall mitigation plans.
Continuous Process Improvement: Drive operational efficiency and take-rate expansion by identifying structural bottlenecks, grounding decisions in rigorous data analysis, and driving initiatives to "build a better machine."
2. Capacity Procurement, Pricing & Solution Design
Export & Import Solutioning: Fully own end-to-end export procurement, routing, and solution design for the region. Partner with overseas/origin air procurement managers to secure competitive import capacity, transit times, and door-to-door pricing tailored to client requirements.
Airline Relationship & Vendor Management: Nurture and leverage executive-level relationships with regional and global airline carriers. Assess carrier performance, enforce service level agreements (SLAs), drive service quality improvements, and coordinate regional air trucking/drayage coverage.
RFQ Sponsorship & Bid Management: Oversee custom door-to-door pricing structures for regional bids. Act as the executive sponsor for high-value global RFQs for top regional accounts, ensuring sharp, market-competitive solutions that protect margins.
Contract Administration & Compliance: Own and manage carrier agreements, block space agreements (BSAs), and spot rates within the internal procurement database to guarantee accurate cost application and rate compliance across systems.
3. Business Development & Commercial Enablement
Go-To-Market (GTM) Strategy: Serve as the default subject-matter expert for regional demand teams. Shape commercial strategies by identifying high-potential target verticals, providing qualified prospect lead lists, and guiding initial outreach.
Client Acquisition & Executive Selling: Actively participate in regional commercial operating rhythms (pipeline reviews, top-of-funnel reviews, district sales meetings). Accompany sales teams on client visits, lead strategic pitch presentations, and help close complex enterprise deals.
Account Retention & Expansion: Partner with Account Management to expand wallet share with existing clients through creative pricing, customized air charter/freight solutions, and proactive relationship management to prevent churn.
Market Intelligence & Communication: Continuously monitor air cargo market dynamics, rate fluctuations, capacity constraints, and competitor positioning. Regularly communicate actionable market insights to local and regional sales organizations.

Apprenticeship & Mentorship: Serve as a cultural pillar by coaching, training, and mentoring local teams across Operations, Customer Service, and Pricing to build deep regional expertise.
Hands-on Operational Escalation: Utilize deep first-hand operational knowledge to step in when needed (troubleshooting quality issues, resolving execution breakdowns, and demonstrating end-to-end shipment handling best practices.)
Internal & External Representation: Represent the Global Air Team in regional executive meetings and represent the company externally at industry conferences, vendor summits, and customer events.

Experience
Industry Experience: 7+ years of experience at a freight forwarder or in a similar field
Solutioning & Pricing Expertise: 5+ years of direct experience designing complex, door-to-door air freight routing solutions and competitive pricing models for enterprise customers of varying sizes.
Commercial & Executive Engagement: Proven track record in business development, senior-level client relationship management, and winning strategic RFQs.
Network & Industry Rolodex: Established relationships with regional and global airline leadership, as well as an active client network within the region (highly preferred).
Skills & Competencies
Financial & Analytical Acumen: Deep understanding of freight forwarding economics, P&L management, yield optimization, and data-driven decision-making.
End-to-End Operational Knowledge: Direct, practical knowledge of air freight operations, TSA/security regulations, cross-border customs, carrier routings, and local drayage workflows.
High Energy & Collaboration: Proactive, highly energetic leader capable of operating seamlessly across time zones, from coordinating with overseas procurement teams at night to negotiating with local vendors and clients during the day.
Communication & Negotiation: Superior verbal, written, and presentation skills with a strong ability to influence internal stakeholders and external executive decision-makers.

We are seeking a Sr. Cost Accountant to join our diverse and discerning finance and accounting team!  Specifically, we are looking for someone who is ready for growth in their career and ready to tackle challenges as the company grows and changes.  Reporting to the Assistant Controller, this role will have extensive opportunities to improve processes and controls; as well as drive efficiencies throughout the cost accounting processes in our flagship, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility.  Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Standard costing and cost accounting
   
   - Develop, maintain, and update standard costs, BOM/routing roll-ups, and labor and overhead rates
   
   - Record and reconcile material, labor, and overhead costs to the general ledger
   
   Work order and variance analysis
   
   - Analyze work orders for cost overruns, yield/scrap, and efficiency issues
   
   - Calculate and explain purchase price, material usage, labor, overhead, and yield variances; identify root causes in partnering with FP&A and Operations.
   
   Inventory and WIP accounting
   
   - Own inventory valuation, roll-forward, and COGS reconciliations
   
   - Evaluate excess and obsolete (E&O) and lower-of-cost-or-NRV reserves
   
   - Collaborate with Warehousing team in their execution of cycle and physical counts, including validation that adjustments made were approved as per the Company’s approval process
   
   Close, reporting, and audit
   
   - Prepare cost-related journal entries, reconciliations, and flux analysis for month-end close
   
   - Support budgeting, forecasting, and product/project profitability analysis
   
   - Provide documentation and support for internal and external audits
   
   Controls and process improvement
   
   - Design, document, and test inventory and cost controls (SOX where applicable)
   
   - Identify opportunities to automate recurring reconciliations, reporting, and variance workflows




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - CPA licensed

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting

 - 3–5 years of progressive US GAAP accounting experience (at least 2 years in public accounting)

 - Experience in a start-up, high-growth, or first-of-a-kind manufacturing environment a plus

 - Hands-on experience with standard costing, BOM/routing cost roll-ups, and inventory valuation

 - Experience with ERP systems (Oracle Fusion a plus) and using AI tools

This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.

title: Head of Sales
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the role
As Head of Sales, you'll own Formic's sales strategy, execution, team performance, and revenue generation results. Your responsibility is to grow and manage a high-performing sales organization that consistently wins new business while concurrently growing and expanding within existing customers.
We're looking for a commercially astute builder who knows how to turn complex customer needs into successful sales. You'll develop a sharp understanding of manufacturers, their operational challenges, and the economics of automation, then use customer insights and performance data to strengthen targeting, sales execution, and growth. You'll be responsible for helping to identify what is working, change what isn’t, and implement effective practices to drive sales success.
You'll lead and develop our Sales team, identifying what makes our best customer engagements and salespeople successful and turning those insights into better coaching, stronger qualification, higher conversion, and more consistent performance. You’ll leverage data and insights derived from Formic’s range of GTM tools and tech stack, customer feedback, and feedback from other Formic teams (i.e Customer Success, Solutions, Service, etc.) to continuously improve the sales process and methodologies to better align with unmet customer need and desired outcomes.  You'll stay close to important deals and help the team navigate operational, financial, and technical stakeholders with confidence.
This is a hands-on leadership role requiring a combination of strategic judgment, direct & active team management, and tactical execution. You'll challenge assumptions, make decisions grounded in data and customer insights, prototype, test, iterate, and ultimately implement changes, and measure their impact quantitatively and qualitatively. Working across the business, you'll build a more effective, predictable, and scalable sales organization.
What You'll Do
Sales strategy and execution
Own sales targets, territory strategy, account prioritization, and revenue performance. Establish clear standards for opportunity ownership, workload distribution, response times, pipeline progression, and follow-through; proactively resolve stalled opportunities, capacity constraints, and performance gaps.
Study target producers and manufacturers, applications, buying processes, and competitive alternatives to focus effort on the best opportunities.
Improve discovery, qualification, business cases, proposals, negotiations, and closing; participate directly in high-stakes deals.
Personally own and drive select sales opportunities each quarter to maintain firsthand knowledge of our customers, product, and sales process.
Establish rapid iteration and testing of new or modified sales approaches and tactics, accounting for differences in regions, markets, and application verticals
Balance customer value, pricing, profitability, technical feasibility, and deployment requirements when evaluating opportunities.
Sales leadership and coaching
Build and lead a disciplined sales management organization. Recruit, develop, and hold accountable sellers and managers; equip regional leads with clear expectations, performance metrics, coaching practices, and the skills to develop their teams while maintaining their own commercial effectiveness.
Use call observation, deal reviews, customer feedback, and performance data to understand why individuals and deals succeed or stall.
Translate top-performer practices into repeatable training, targeted coaching, and stronger team-wide performance.
Validate impacts and results of training, coaching, and enablement to ensure the team’s performance is quantitatively improving as a result.
Sales operations and collaboration
Build reliable forecasting, CRM discipline, meaningful metrics, and operating routines that surface opportunities and risks early.
Improve sales processes, tools, reporting, and resource allocation; test changes and measure their impact.
Establish a disciplined operating partnership with Marketing and Sales Development, jointly refining the ideal customer profile, account priorities, qualification standards, opportunity handoffs, sales follow-through, and feedback from won and lost deals to improve pipeline quality and conversion.
Coordinate with Solutions, Engineering, Operations, and Customer Success on feasibility, customer commitments, and handoffs. Own commercial execution for expansion within existing accounts, partnering with Customer Success to surface whitespace, prioritize opportunities, and ensure accountable follow-through.
What makes you a great fit
Curiosity and a demonstrated desire to learn and serve customers
Demonstrated success building sales capabilities, operating rhythms, and team performance in a growing B2B business, including driving process change and improvements while ensuring existing momentum is maintained
Exceptional coach who diagnoses performance gaps and helps people improve through direct feedback and practical training.
Experience leading consultative sales of complex technical or operational solutions, navigating plant-level stakeholders, financial decision-makers, implementation considerations, and extended sales cycles.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including pipeline analysis, forecasting, deal economics, and Salesforce or similar CRM tools.
Hands-on, resourceful leader who can build processes, recruit talent, make difficult decisions, and close important deals.
Experience selling hardware or equipment into manufacturing operations is a plus.
What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.
Equal Opportunity Employment:
Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to accessibility@formic.co .
AI Use:
At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked  here .

title: Service Technician II
description:
Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
The Service/Repair Technician 2 possesses fundamental knowledge and has demonstrated mechanical and electrical aptitude with troubleshooting experience. Responsible for providing on-site support to Hobart Service customers that includes but is not limited to: installation and/ or service of commercial food equipment. Routine work schedule including on-call, after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-site repair support.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES FOR ALL TECHNICIAN LEVELS
These are the most significant job duties performed. The size, scope and complexity of assigned duties and responsibilities are dependent on the level and experience of the incumbent. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each assigned essential duty satisfactorily. Other responsibilities or special projects not specifically listed below may also be assigned.
Installs mechanical and electrical commercial food equipment and assists in more advanced installs as needed.
Maintain, diagnose, and repair basic mechanical commercial food equipment for customers on contract and/or on time and material (i.e., T&M) basis.
Ability to interpret and follow schematic diagrams.
Demonstrate knowledge of sequence of operations for multiple operating modes.
Completes and documents preventative maintenance on mechanical and electrical commercial food equipment.
Implements and supports standard operating procedures outlined in Hobart Service safety manuals and programs.
Supports branch and organization financial objectives by providing a quality customer experience.
Maintains current organization, industry, and equipment knowledge.
Responsible for assigned company assets including vehicle, tools, and inventory.
Follows the company's safe driving and other applicable policies.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Education and Work Experience
High school diploma or GED and 2-4 years of electrical and mechanical experience, or
High school diploma or GED and 0-2 years of HVACR service experience with an EPA certification, or
Vocational certificate in HVACR
Desired Education/Experience
Associate’s degree or Vocational Certificate is preferred.
Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing commercial cooking and/or refrigeration equipment is preferred.
Certificates and Licenses
Position/Location dependent. Industry certification is highly desirable.
Job Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
Mechanical Aptitude – demonstrates mechanical and electrical aptitude to operate and troubleshoot equipment. Skilled in use of various tools and equipment (e.g. basic hand tools, reading and following service manuals, gauges, meters, etc.)
Customer Service - highly professional demeanor with excellent telephone skills and etiquette. Utilizes various interpersonal styles and communication methods to positively assist and influence customers.
Problem Solving - fundamental role in finding ways to address all types of problems by having a good approach to a problem without being ineffective, favoring or causing painful consequences.
Safety at Work - learns to keep the organization safe from different risks by developing a high sense of alertness that detects danger from afar and stops it before it causes risk, danger or injury to themselves, or others.

Technical and Analytical Skills
Ability to read and interpret standard service manuals, mechanical diagrams, sustains understanding of parts stocking and identification methods, practices, and procedures.
Understanding of basic math (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, calculations of percentages, measurement conversions).
Compiles and summarizes data for supervisor and/or branch manager that will help him/her with creating customer-focused strategies for fostering relationships a nd sales (e.g., equipment leads, contract leads, water treatment order leads).
Basic knowledge of / working knowledge of Windows applications and Microsoft Office programs such as Word and Excel.

Applies feedback to improve performance.
Monitors own work to ensure quality.

Works quickly.

Demonstrates a comprehensive knowledge of company products and services.
Completes required safety training.

Occasional roof access may be necessary through extension ladders or fixed ladders greater than 20 feet

Job Description:
The Senior Manufacturing Engineer role is presented with the opportunity to solve complex manufacturing challenges, improve fabrication and machining processes, and influence manufacturing performance.  The individual will provide an advanced level of expertise in manufacturing through strategic planning, organization, control, integration and completion of assigned responsibilities by coordinating with engineering team members and operations management.  The Senior Manufacturing Engineer coordinates implementation of capex projects and is ultimately responsible for all aspects of the project including budgeting, cost estimation, developing project timelines and transitioning projects to manufacturing.   The Senior Manufacturing Engineer must possess a strong understanding and background in fabricated assemblies, welding processes, and machining. Reporting to the Manufacturing Engineering Manager, the Senior Manufacturing Engineer is responsible for providing technical leadership to engineering support roles to drive new product development initiatives and operation improvement within the organization.
Essential Functions :

Coordinated justification of capital projects, balancing production impact, business needs, and timing in partnership with the Operations team.

Identify and lead implementation of cost takeout opportunities through waste reduction, material substitutions and equipment modifications.
Ability to make independent decisions and regularly suggest ways to improve services & processes
Engenders trust to influence without authority at all levels of the organization
Mentors to strengthen skill sets of indirect reports and assist in the talent development activities to ensure a strong pipeline of talent
Coordinate internal resources and third parties / vendors for the flawless execution of projects

Lead process standardization efforts for safety, service, quality and cost

Uses appropriate verification techniques to manage changes in project scope, schedule, and costs

Maintain knowledge of manufacturing processes to improve competitive position
Apply ITW Lean Operating Principles to manufacturing operations

title: Third Shift Lead Process Technician
description:
Job Description:
ITW's Lakeville, CT facility is seeking an experienced 3rd Shift Lead Process Technician to join our manufacturing team.
We are a clean, modern, fully in-line, highly automated Automotive manufacturing facility utilizing state-of-the-art injection molding equipment, robotics, automated material handling, and advanced vision inspection systems.
The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with plastic injection molding processes, injection mold tooling, and hot runner systems. Experience with automation and robotic systems is highly desirable.
This position will serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing, providing direction, supervision, and mentorship to machine operators while ensuring production requirements, quality standards, and equipment performance are consistently maintained.
The successful candidate must obtain strong communication skills, possess excellent mechanical aptitude, and demonstrate the ability to independently troubleshoot processing and equipment issues while effectively leading the production team.
This is a hands-on leadership position requiring a balance of technical process knowledge, equipment setup & troubleshooting, production oversight, and team leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Injection Molding Process & Equipment
Set up, start up, and optimize injection molding processes to meet production and quality requirements.
Monitor and maintain process parameters to ensure consistent part quality and production efficiency.
Troubleshoot injection molding process issues, including short shots, flash, dimensional variation, cosmetic defects, and other quality-related concerns.
Demonstrate a strong understanding of injection molds, mold construction, and hot runner systems.
Perform mold changes, process setups, and equipment adjustments as required.
Identify opportunities to improve cycle times, scrap reduction, and improve overall equipment performance.
Work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance to resolve process and equipment-related issues.
Ensure all production equipment is cleaned, maintained, operating safely and efficiently
Monitor and support Wittmann Battenfeld, Nissei & Toshiba injection molding machines.
Automation & Advanced Manufacturing Technology
Support the operation, setup, and troubleshooting of Wittmann robotic equipment.
Support Wittmann central material feeding systems and auxiliary equipment.
Monitor and troubleshoot automated material handling systems and associated equipment.
Support and troubleshoot Keyence vision inspection systems used to identify part defects and quality-related issues.
Ensure automated inspection systems are functioning properly and identify potential quality concerns.
Work with Maintenance and Engineering to resolve molding & automation-related downtime and equipment issues.
Third Shift Leadership & Production Support
Serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing operations.
Supervise, direct, and mentor machine operators to ensure production expectations are met.
Provide technical guidance and support to operators when processing or equipment issues arise.
Monitor production performance, scrap, downtime, and overall shift efficiency.
Ensure operators follow established work instructions, quality requirements, and safety procedures.
Communicate production concerns, equipment issues, quality problems, and outstanding maintenance needs to the appropriate personnel and incoming shifts.
Maintain accurate production records shift end emails and shift reports.
Escalate issues appropriately and ensure timely resolution of production concerns.
Promote accountability, teamwork, and a positive working environment.
Communication & Documentation
Maintain strong communication with production leadership, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, and other departments.
Provide detailed and accurate shift handoff information to ensure production continuity.
Utilize Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word, for production documentation and reporting.
Utilize Microsoft Outlook for professional communication and coordination.
Maintain accurate records of production issues, downtime. scrap, and process changes.
Additional Responsibilities
Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned to support manufacturing operations and business needs.
Required Qualifications
Previous 5+ years' experience as a Process Technician in a plastic injection molding manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of injection molding processes and process optimization.
Experience working with injection molds and hot runner systems.
Demonstrated troubleshooting skills involving molding processes, equipment, and quality-related issues.
Ability to identify and resolve processing issues independently.
Strong mechanical aptitude and hands-on troubleshooting abilities.
Previous experience providing technical direction, leading, supervising, or mentoring production personnel.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Outlook.
Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Strong commitment to safety, quality, production efficiency, and continuous improvement.
Preferred Qualifications - Automation & Equipment
Experience or familiarity with the following equipment and technologies is a plus:
Wittmann Robots: Experience with robotic setup, operation, and troubleshooting.
Wittmann Battenfeld, Nissei, & Toshiba Injection Molding Machines: Experience with machine setup, operation, and process troubleshooting.
Keyence Vision Systems: Familiarity with camera inspection systems used for automated part inspection and defect detection is a plus.
Employee Benefits
ITW offers competitive compensation and an excellent benefits package, including:
Medical Insurance
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance
Company-Matched 401(k) Retirement Plan
Employee discounts on qualifying products and services.
Discounts on participating parks, entertainment, and shows.
Paid time off, sick time, short- and long-term disability, & paid holidays.
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Process Technician looking to take the next step into a shift leadership role within a modern, highly automated manufacturing facility.
If you have a strong background in injection molding, hot runner systems, automation, and production leadership, we encourage you to apply.

$33/hour + 10% shift differential = $36.30/hour

Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.

Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

description:

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The opportunity:
Advancing minimally invasive care requires more than great technology — it requires people who grow with the company, lead with intention, and bring their best to every challenge. The Director, Enterprise Learning will shape how we build capability from the inside out: ensuring every employee, manager, and director has the knowledge, skills, and mindset to perform and grow.
We're looking for someone who sees learning as a business discipline, not a support function. Someone who starts with strategy — understanding where Intuitive is headed and what capabilities will get us there — and works backward to design learning that actually moves the needle. A builder who combines learning design expertise with sharp business judgment, and who knows how to measure whether any of it is working.
This role covers role agnostic enterprise learning below the VP level: individual contributor development, manager learning, director learning, and employee onboarding. It's a broad remit that requires both vision and execution — and a leader who can do both.
What you'll lead:
You'll report directly to the VP, Global Talent and own the strategy, design, and delivery of enterprise-wide learning programs that are connected to business priorities, deliver measurable impact, and built to last. This isn't about building a curriculum library — it's about building capability that shows up in business results.
What this looks like:
Anchor learning to business strategy. Partner closely with HR Business Partners, business leaders, and the broader Talent team to understand where the company is going and what capabilities will be required to get there. Translate that into a multi-year enterprise learning strategy with clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and a coherent point of view on what we build, buy, or curate.
Design learning that works. Lead the design and delivery of learning experiences across the full employee population — from onboarding through director-level development. Apply modern instructional design principles across a range of modalities: in-person, digital, cohort-based, on-demand, and AI-enabled. Prioritize approaches that fit how people actually learn at work.
Own manager and director development. Build and continuously evolve learning programs for managers and directors that are practical, relevant, and grounded in what Intuitive needs from its people leaders. Work closely with HR Business Partners to ensure programs address real capability gaps, not just generic leadership topics.
Deliver a best-in-class onboarding experience. Design and steward an onboarding experience that accelerates time-to-productivity, connects new employees to Intuitive's mission and culture, and sets a strong foundation for long-term engagement and performance.
Make learning measurable. Define clear success metrics for every major program and build the infrastructure to track them. Move beyond attendance and satisfaction scores — connect learning outcomes to performance, retention, and business impact. Use data to make honest calls about what's working and what isn't.
Bring modern learning approaches to life. Stay close to how the learning landscape is evolving — AI-enabled personalization, digital learning platforms, cohort learning, nudge-based reinforcement — and bring the right innovations into Intuitive in ways that are practical and scalable, not just novel.
Build and lead a high-performing team. Lead a team of learning professionals with clarity, high standards, and genuine investment in their development. Create an environment where craft matters, outcomes are tracked, and continuous improvement is the norm.
Partner across HR and the business. Work closely with Talent Management, HR Business Partners, People Analytics, and I&D to ensure enterprise learning is integrated into the broader talent strategy — and that programs reflect and reinforce an inclusive, high-performance culture.
Design and lead manager enablement strategies and programs that equip leaders with the tools, resources, and capabilities to effectively lead and develop their teams.
Design and lead AI enablement and literacy initiatives that build employee confidence, accelerate responsible adoption, and help teams effectively integrate AI into their day-to-day work.
Qualifications
What you'll bring:
Learning strategy and design expertise: Significant experience designing and delivering enterprise learning programs across multiple audiences and modalities — from onboarding through senior individual contributors and people leaders. You understand instructional design deeply and apply it with both rigor and pragmatism.
Business acumen: You think like a business leader. You understand how Intuitive creates value, what's driving the strategy, and how to connect learning investments to business outcomes. You can hold your own in conversations with senior leaders about priorities, trade-offs, and ROI.
Modern learning fluency: Genuine familiarity with the evolving learning landscape — AI-enabled learning tools, digital platforms, cohort-based models, on-demand content strategies, and data-driven personalization. You know what's worth adopting and how to bring it in thoughtfully.
Measurement and outcomes orientation: A track record of defining meaningful success metrics for learning programs and using data to drive decisions. You're not satisfied with completion rates — you want to know whether learning changed behavior and moved business results.
Stakeholder influence: Strong ability to build relationships with and influence senior business leaders and HR partners. You can translate learning strategy into language that resonates with business audiences, and you earn credibility through follow-through and results.
People leadership: You lead with clarity and high standards, invest genuinely in your team's growth, and create an environment where excellent work is the expectation.
Operational excellence: You can manage a complex portfolio of programs, vendors, and priorities without losing sight of quality. You build systems and processes that scale — and you know when to simplify.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in Learning & Development, Organizational Psychology, Instructional Design, or a related field preferred.
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise learning, with demonstrated success leading learning strategy and design across a large, complex organization.
Experience with AI-enabled learning tools and modern digital learning platforms strongly preferred.
Ability to travel approximately 20% of the time.

Primary Function of Position
The Senior Epidemiologist, Real-World Evidence Generation will design and execute data-driven analyses
using claims databases and real-world evidence to demonstrate the clinical and economic value of
emerging robotic platforms. This role focuses on rigorous statistical analysis of U.S. commercial and
Medicare claims data, real-world outcomes research, and translating findings into evidence that supports
regulatory submissions, payer discussions, and clinical adoption. The successful candidate will combine
epidemiologic expertise with advanced statistical methods to generate peer-reviewed publications and
evidence dossiers that demonstrate procedure value and patient benefit.
Essential Job Duties
• Real-World Evidence Generation & Claims Data Analysis
• Design and execute comprehensive analyses using U.S. commercial claims databases (e.g.,
MarketScan, Optum), Medicare data, and other population-level observational datasets to
evaluate procedure outcomes, safety, and resource utilization.
• Develop and apply rigorous epidemiologic and statistical methods (descriptive, analytic, causal
inference techniques) to real-world data to characterize patient populations, identify responder
phenotypes, and quantify procedure value.
• Build and document complex research datasets by integrating multi-source claims data (medical,
pharmaceutical, facility claims) with appropriate data governance and quality assurance
protocols.
• Conduct comparative effectiveness research, cost analysis, and health outcomes assessment
using claims-based methodologies.
• Ensure compliance with data use agreements, privacy regulations, and analytical standards in all
database projects.
Statistical Analysis & Methodology
• Perform advanced statistical analyses including logistic regression, survival analysis, propensity
score matching, instrumental variable analysis, and other causal inference methods appropriate
for observational data.
Develop and document standardized analytical code libraries
(SAS, R, SQL) that enable reproducible, transparent research and
support collaboration across teams.
• Apply epidemiologic principles to address confounding, selection
bias, and other threats to validity in observational research.
• Interpret complex statistical findings and communicate results clearly to both technical and non-
technical audiences.
Health Economics Integration
• Support health economic analyses by providing clinical outcome data, cost drivers, and utilization
patterns derived from claims databases.
• Partner with HEOR colleagues to integrate real-world evidence with economic models, ensuring
clinical parameters reflect actual patient populations and healthcare system utilization.
• Quantify resource utilization, cost burden, and clinical benefits for target patient populations
using claims-based metrics.
• Contribute epidemiologic and statistical expertise to develop value propositions grounded in
evidence.
Evidence Translation, Publication Strategy & External Scientific Engagement
• Lead peer-reviewed publication development for real-world evidence studies, ensuring
methodologic rigor and clinical relevance.
• Translate research findings into clear, evidence-based value dossiers and briefing documents for
regulatory, payer, and clinical stakeholders.
• Communicate complex methodologic approaches and findings to diverse audiences through
publications, regulatory submissions, and scientific presentations.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align evidence generation with regulatory pathways
and market access objectives.
• Identify and establish relationships with key opinion leaders and clinical experts relevant to
procedural outcomes and value demonstration.
• Develop publication roadmaps in collaboration with identified KOLs to ensure real-world
evidence reaches target clinical audiences and informs procedural adoption.
• Partner with KOLs on evidence interpretation and manuscript development to strengthen
methodologic rigor, clinical relevance, and impact of findings.
• Lead strategic positioning of real-world evidence findings at key conferences, in high-impact
peer-reviewed journals, and through clinical society engagement to build procedural credibility.
• Support advisory activities and collaborative research initiatives with clinical thought leaders that
align with evidence generation priorities and external validation.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work with Clinical Affairs, Regulatory, and Market Access teams to identify key evidence gaps
and prioritize analyses that support product value demonstration.
• Partner with R&D and Product Management to inform design considerations and clinical
endpoints based on real-world data insights.
• Mentor and support junior analysts and team members in epidemiologic and statistical methods.
• Engage with external stakeholders (KOLs, clinicians, researchers) to validate findings and ensure
clinical relevance.
Required Skills and Experience
4+ years of experience in epidemiologic research, real-world
evidence generation, or outcomes research, with demonstrated
expertise in claims database analysis
• Advanced proficiency in statistical programming languages (R,
SAS, SQL) and experience building and managing large, complex datasets from multiple sources
• Direct experience accessing, analyzing, and interpreting U.S. commercial and Medicare claims
databases (e.g., MarketScan, Optum, Komodo, CMS data)
• Strong knowledge of epidemiologic study designs, causal inference methods, and statistical
approaches for observational data
• Track record of peer-reviewed publications demonstrating methodologic rigor and clinical impact
• Proven ability to work independently on complex analyses while collaborating effectively with
cross-functional teams
• Strong communication skills with ability to translate statistical findings for diverse stakeholder
groups
• Experience working in fast-paced, innovation-driven environments within medical device,
biotech, or health technology sectors
Required Education and Training
Advanced degree in Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Statistics, or related quantitative field (PhD,
MSc strongly preferred); MD/DO with substantial epidemiologic or clinical research background may be
considered

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team leverages and advances the cutting-edge of technology to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the da Vinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Senior Systems Analyst you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This position is the software-oriented track within Systems Analysis, bridging the team’s algorithms and the software infrastructure they run on. You will own the software layer between the application and the real-time control loop, the bring-up of the embedded compute platform, the software side of the FPGA interface, and you will bring enough fluency in control algorithms to connect their signals to the right system modes and safety responses. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.
Essential Job Duties
•       Design, implement, and own the software layer between the application software and the real-time control loop.
•       Bring up the embedded compute platform and real-time execution environment for new prototype systems.
•       Own the software interface to the FPGA, including drivers and data paths between processors and FPGA logic.
•       Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems and lead embedded bring-up of new manipulators, instruments, and controller boards.
•       Implement control and safety algorithms developed with Systems Analysts as deterministic, production-quality embedded software.
•       Design and implement servo control systems with Systems Analysts, applying control theory to mechatronic and tele-robotic platforms.
•       Connect algorithm signals to the appropriate system modes and safety responses in partnership with the Systems Analysts who own the supervisory logic.
•       Root-cause problems that cross the hardware, software, and control boundary.
•       Develop test, continuous integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure for Systems Analysis software; provide tool building for other engineering issues.
•       Document software design, risks, requirements, and test protocols; document and communicate intellectual property.
•       Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
•       Communicate system performance to the organization and support it as products evolve from design engineering to manufacturing.
•       Act as an interface between Systems Analysis and Software Engineering; take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries.
Required Skills and Experience
•       Strong embedded development skills, including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++, and experience with unit testing, continuous integration, and modern build systems.
•       Experience developing software under real-time constraints, with a solid understanding of determinism, latency, and execution-time analysis.
•       Experience with embedded architectures on multi-processor SoC/FPGA platforms, including bare-metal or RTOS development, device drivers, and inter-processor communication.
•       Hands-on experience bringing up embedded platforms and integrating prototype hardware with software.
•       Working knowledge of control systems and robotics sufficient to read, modify, and reason about control code and its timing.
•       MATLAB and Python programming capabilities for analysis, simulation, and tool building.
•       Comfort with the concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
•       Detail-oriented, with the ability to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
•       Hands-on engineering experience with a proven ability to work well in a team environment.
•       Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
•       A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives.
Required Education and Training
•       Minimum MS degree in CS, EE, ME, or a similar field with 4–5+ years of industrial experience, or a PhD with 1–3+ years of experience, or a BS with 7+ years of relevant industrial experience.
Working Conditions
•       Position is primarily office/lab-based (Sunnyvale, CA). Requires regular access to prototype and lab environments with standard safety precautions. Up to 10% travel for clinical site visits, partner meetings, or conference participation.
Preferred Skills and Experience
•       Experience designing and implementing servo control systems, or a deeper robotics and controls background.
•       Medical device or safety-critical system product experience (FDA design controls, ISO 13485, ISO 14971).
•       Experience with surgical robotics, haptics, or tele-presence system design.
•       Familiarity with FPGA-based motor control or other embedded real-time architectures.
•       Experience developing products in a highly regulated environment, including through FDA clearance.

Provide daily engineering support for existing in-house manufacturing lines.

Abhility to lift, maneuver, and troubleshoot fixtures and tools

Container and orchestration security

title: Director, Internal Controls
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
The Director of Internal Controls will build and lead a practical, business-focused enterprise internal control and risk management program that supports Invenergy’s continued growth. This role will partner directly with leaders across finance, accounting, technology, legal, compliance, development, construction, and operations to identify and assess significant risks, establish scalable controls, strengthen process documentation, and promote clear ownership and accountability.
The Director will be a hands-on leader who can set the strategy, develop the program, and work alongside the business to provide practical, risk-based guidance and maintain an effective, sustainable control environment as the organization evolves.
Responsibilities
Build and lead a formal annual enterprise risk assessment process that identifies significant risks across the organization, evaluates their relative likelihood and impact, and maps the controls intended to mitigate those risks.
Incorporate fraud risk into the annual assessment, including potential fraud schemes, incentives and opportunities, management override, and the preventive and detective controls needed to address those risks.
Maintain a practical, formally documented risk and internal control inventory that identifies each objective, associated risk, control activity, owner, and frequency, and ensure it is updated as the business, systems, risks, and processes change.
Ensure key processes and controls are supported by approved, usable procedures that define the control objective, execution steps, frequency, preparer, reviewer, exception handling, escalation, and required evidence.
Develop a scalable internal control framework and operating model that reflects Invenergy’s ownership structure, business complexity, growth plans, and risk profile.
Work directly with business and functional leaders to establish clear accountability and design controls that are effective, efficient, and integrated into day-to-day operations.
Perform and oversee periodic reviews of control design and operation, identify gaps, agree on practical corrective actions with management, and monitor remediation through completion.
Challenge existing processes constructively and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and strengthen controls while supporting speed, accountability, and business growth.
Establish and maintain formal internal audit procedures, including a risk-based annual audit plan, scoping, planning, fieldwork, sampling, testing, documentation, quality review, reporting, issue rating, management responses, remediation follow-up, and escalation.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity for internal audit activities and coordinate efficiently with external auditors, legal, compliance, technology, and other assurance partners.
Provide concise, decision-useful reporting to senior management and other governance stakeholders on key risks, control coverage, audit results, open issues, remediation progress, and emerging concerns.
Serve as a trusted advisor to management on new initiatives, acquisitions, systems, and process changes so that appropriate controls are considered early and scaled to the underlying risk.
Build risk and control awareness across the organization through practical training, clear guidance, and regular communication with control owners.
Develop the internal controls function over time, including setting priorities, managing resources, developing talent, and maintaining a multi-year roadmap aligned with the company’s needs.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in accounting.
10+ years of progressive experience in internal controls, internal audit, enterprise risk management, compliance, public accounting, or a related field, including experience working directly with senior business leaders.
Demonstrated experience building or improving risk assessments, risk and control inventories, process documentation, and internal audit or control monitoring programs.
Strong understanding of risk and internal control principles, including fraud risk, control design, issue evaluation, remediation, and managing controls through business and system change.
Proven ability to operate strategically and tactically, build a function from the ground up, and translate risk concepts into practical processes that business teams can own and sustain.
Strong judgment, curiosity, leadership, project management, and written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to succeed in an entrepreneurial, fast-paced, and collaborative environment with evolving priorities, limited bureaucracy, and a high degree of personal accountability.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
CPA, CIA, CISA, or other relevant professional certification preferred.
Big four public accounting experience preferred.
Experience applying COSO or similar frameworks in a practical, risk-based manner appropriate for a growing, operationally complex organization.
Experience in the energy, power generation, infrastructure, construction, or renewable energy industries.
Experience with governance, risk, and compliance tools, data analytics, technology-enabled controls, and control automation.
Experience building or transforming an internal controls or internal audit function in a growing complex company.

Job Description
Job Purpose
This is a Research and Development (R&D) role within the Central Ingredients, Analytical, and Nutrition Sciences organization on the Global Sweetener & Salt - Science & Technology team, based at the Kraft Heinz Innovation Center in Glenview, Illinois. The role supports innovative and disruptive ingredient research that creates competitive advantage across the global Kraft Heinz portfolio. The Associate Scientist will lead and support prototype development, validate technology in model systems and applications, support and conduct technology scale-up trials, prepare and analyze samples, and support processes that commercialize technologies. The work includes understanding business needs, designing and performing tests, analyzing data, drawing conclusions, documenting work, and communicating results to technical and non-technical audiences. The role requires a technical background, problem-solving and project management skills, general food science and ingredient knowledge, and the ability to manage assignments with a high degree of autonomy. Experience with flavor, taste, sweetener ingredient technologies, and sodium reduction is preferred. Intellectual curiosity, comfort with ambiguity, collaboration, and strong communication are essential.

Design, support, and complete benchtop and/or pilot plant trials, and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical teams.
Connect and direct communication with suppliers to acquire the materials necessary for research.
Complete internal research projects with some supervision, coaching, and training, while demonstrating the ability to work independently and take initiative to consult with other scientists.
Work with cross-functional teams to support projects from concept through commercialization, including Marketing, Operations, Quality, External Manufacturers, and Procurement.
Help maintain a clean and functional laboratory space.
Prepare samples and conduct sample analysis.
Participate in and embrace all aspects of ingredient technology development, including the fuzzy front end, conceptualization, design, development, and commercialization.

Clear research summaries and translations of findings for technical and non-technical teams.
Proof-of-concept formulations and product-development work across multiple categories.
Completed benchtop and/or pilot plant trials with clearly communicated results.
Prepared and analyzed samples that support ingredient research.
Ingredient technologies supported from conceptualization and development through commercialization.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
B.S. degree in Food Science, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or a related field.
Ingredient and food matrix/model system knowledge.
Experience with flavor, taste, sweetener ingredient technologies, sodium reduction, and applications is preferred.
Familiarity with and understanding of Design of Experiments, laboratory experimentation, laboratory equipment, scale-up, and mathematical/data analysis.
Demonstrated record of conducting research and development projects individually or in collaboration with other teams.
Willingness and ability to learn new product categories; experience across multiple product categories is a plus.
Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity.
Demonstrated track record of creative, out-of-the-box problem solving.
Experience interacting with suppliers.
Strong written and verbal communication, interpersonal, and project management skills.
Ability to build strong relationships and networks internally and externally.

This role is based at the Kraft Heinz Innovation Center in Glenview, Illinois. Traveling up to 20% is required. Additionally, this role requires at minimum 3 days in office and 2 days remote .
