Job Purpose
The R&D Scientist for Data Analytics & Operations uses R&D-owned data and technical knowledge to deliver accurate, actionable analysis that supports business decisions across business areas such as carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). This position keeps that data accurate, consistent, traceable and accessible for use across enterprise systems and digital solutions through stewardship, governance and documentation, and helps prepare it for use in a variety of digital tools and solutions. Working with regular guidance alongside Procurement, Corporate ESG, digital and other partners, the role represents North America R&D in enterprise sustainability and compliance initiatives, serving as a trusted link between R&D subject-matter expertise and cross-functional teams. It suits data professionals with food or CPG experience as well as food or packaging scientists with strong data skills.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Steward R&D data by investigating data-quality issues, reconciling discrepancies and keeping data accurate, consistent, and reliable across sources.
​Support data governance by applying established standards and maintaining definitions, mappings, taxonomy, metadata, validation checks and traceable documentation, flagging gaps to data owners
​Help prepare, structure and validate R&D data and content for ingestion into enterprise data platforms and downstream applications
​Query, combine and analyze R&D-owned product, ingredient, packaging and nutrition data to identify trends and deliver recurring reporting and analysis, for example carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting such as EPR
​Provide business requirements and validation criteria for automated, self-service and AI-enabled data solutions, and support testing for accuracy and relevance
​Use analytics to assess the impact of ingredient, packaging, specification or process changes across the portfolio by identifying affected products, technical dependencies and information gaps
​Participate in organizational sustainability and compliance initiatives, such as emissions-reduction and packaging programs, on behalf of North America R&D, contributing technical input and gathering information from R&D colleagues
​Collaborate with a wide range of cross-functional teams, support the use of relevant tools, data and guidance, and translate complex information for technical and non-technical partners ​
Manage multiple assignments across topic areas with regular guidance, moving between broad coverage and focused analysis as assignments require, prioritizing deliverables and escalating questions, risks and issues appropriately

The Kraft Heinz Company manufactures and markets food and beverage products in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, Australia and throughout Asia-Pacific. Our products include condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, coffee, and other grocery products, as well as infant and nutrition products.
As one of the world’s largest food and beverage companies, we are proud to spark joy around mealtimes with a global portfolio of more than 200 brands. Our iconic brands include Kraft, Oscar Mayer, Heinz, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Maxwell House, Capri Sun, Kool-Aid, Jell-O, and Classico, among others. And we also stand committed to sustainability, and the health of our planet and its people. Every day, we are transforming the food industry with bold thinking and unprecedented results. title: Controls Technician
description:
Job Description:
Mars Snacking - Controls Technician - TNN
Area: 3
Hiring Manager: Scott Walther
Shift Schedule: Rotating night shift 2-2-3
Hours: 6:45 AM - 7:15 PM (Must be flexible pending business needs).
The Controls Technician will maintain, adjust, troubleshoot and repair electrical equipment such as motors, motor control circuits, power distribution systems up to 480 VAC, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC's focusing on Rockwell and Siemens) and AC/DC drives. The incumbent must be capable of using electrical test equipment, meters, o-scopes, etc., and possess the skills required to troubleshoot to a component level.  Additional requirements include knowledge of robotics, automated processes, and photoelectric and ultrasonic sensors.  The incumbent must also be able to read wiring diagrams and schematics and understand the software associated with PLC's in order to troubleshoot issues.  In addition, the incumbent assists the Maintenance Mechanics when troubleshooting issues.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications :
Obtain line manager approval.
Meet the required time-in-role criteria
Maintain good standing status (See definition below).
High school diploma and minimum of three to five years' experience in a TPM/technical, manufacturing environment.
Preferred Qualifications :
A technical degree in Industrial Maintenance, Electrical/Controls or related engineering/technical fields.
Physical Requirements :
Perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.
Frequent lifting/carrying (10–50 lbs) and pushing/pulling (50–300 lbs).
Frequent bending, stooping, twisting, handling, and gripping.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Responsible for the maintenance and troubleshooting of electrical and control systems equipment down to the component level, including 480V electrical power distribution, instrumentation, motor controls, VFD’s, Servo’s, I/O devices/modules, PLC’s, HMI’s, and control networks.
Troubleshoot machine breakdowns and malfunctions utilizing a working knowledge of control system programs and tools required to troubleshoot PLC’s, HMI’s, and VFD/servo systems including electrical schematics, programming software, meters, and other electrical test equipment.
Repair, replace and calibrate all electrical sensing devices, instrumentation including photoelectric, inductive, capacitive, pressure, temperature, weight, position sensors, flow, and analytical instruments.
Coordinate the electrical preventative maintenance program by identifying items that need regular inspection and replacement, scheduling the tasks and task frequencies required, and following up to ensure the completion and effectiveness of each task.
Manage all PLC, Servo and HMI programs and changes as well as electrical documentation.  Ensure that they are all accurate, updated, and available to the technicians and archived at regular intervals.
Other job duties as assigned by your Line Manager.
What can you expect from Mars?
The opportunity to learn and develop, taking charge of your own career across Mars.
An industry-competitive salary and great benefits package.
The chance to work cross-functionally and add value and impact to the business.
If you are passionate, a great problem solver, resilient, and have a high drive for results, then we want to hear from you!
*“Good standing” for these purposes is defined as performance rated better than Unsatisfactory in the prior and current year and not on a Performance Improvement Plan or Off-Track at the time of application and no active documented written warnings.

The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.
Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that TSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions, enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, TSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).  elving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.

description:
Job Description:
Sales Analyst, Sam’s Club – Mars Snacking
Bentonville, AR
The Sales/Customer Analyst, Sam’s Club is responsible for enabling the customer team with full analytical support for the Mars Wrigley business. This role is expected to create, deliver and maintain reporting and analysis in support of the customer team to deliver objectives of revenue, growth, profit, product/assortment, placement/everyday shelving, merchandising, pricing and promotions.This role will interact cross functionally with the Sam's Club Sales, Supply. Digital, Customer Marketing & Planning and Demand Planning teams. This role requires strong functional and technical skills, analytical and financial acumen, planning and organizational skills and leveraging data and insights to generate actionable results.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree
2 years Business Analytics experience preferably in Sales, Category Management, Operations, and/or Finance
Proficient in Microsoft Word, Power Point and Excel
Ability to travel 15% of the time
Preferred Qualifications:
3+ years Business Analytics experience preferably in Sales, Category Management, Operations, and/or Finance
CPG Industry experience
Strong Analytical Skills
MBA or Advanced degree
What would be your key responsibilities?
With full understanding of the annual customer business planning, customer solutions and company objectives, this role enables the customer team in all activity by:
Creating and producing reports to perform a wide range of analytics that drive insights and actionable items to be used by customer team
Assembling analysis/reports from multiple data sources (Nielsen, Madrid, Retail Link, Compass) that tracks achievement, yields insights and supports the development of customer solutions that benefits customer and company
Seeking ways (projects) to deliver continual improvement in the process (better, faster) that deliver data that leads to action that builds the business, prevents issues and advances decision making
Developing expertise in leveraging available tools and processes
Developing processes that deliver required analysis timely and effectively (both routine analysis and special analysis); support fact-based information needed by customer team
Being a communication link between internal and external partners; represent customer team at appropriate internal meetings and/or customer meetings

title: Senior Customer Manager, Walmart
description:
Job Description:
The Senior Customer Manager, Walmar t plays a critical role in accelerating growth for the Mars Snacking Chocolate business through the development and execution of customer-centric strategies and annual business plans.
This role leads Walmart account strategy across the Immediate and Future Consumption portfolios, identifying opportunities to expand market share, strengthen customer relationships, and deliver profitable growth.
What Will Be Your Key Responsibilities?
Lead the development and execution of customer strategies and annual business plans that deliver sustainable, profitable growth with Walmart.
Manage Trade, Marketing, Retail Media, and Logistics investments to deliver mutually beneficial business outcomes.
Serve as the voice of the customer on the Walmart leadership team, influencing priorities, investment decisions, and long-term business strategy.
Establish a clear strategic vision for the business and lead execution against key growth, share, and profitability objectives.
Own gross and net revenue forecasting, trade investment management, and delivery of financial commitments in partnership with Finance, Revenue Growth Management, and Sales Planning.
Evaluate customer opportunities and investment decisions through both growth and profitability lenses, balancing volume, share, margin, trade efficiency, and long-term strategic value.
Lead cross-functional collaboration across Sales, Category Management, Marketing, Supply Chain, Customer Service, and Revenue Growth Management to drive best-in-class customer execution.
Develop talent and foster a high-performing team culture by establishing clear priorities, driving engagement, and supporting ongoing career development.
What Are We Looking For?
5+ years of experience building collaborative partnerships with retail customers and cross-functional stakeholders.
Walmart customer management experience strongly preferred.
Proven direct selling and category management experience, with the ability to develop and execute multi-year growth strategies.
Experience leveraging retailer and syndicated data sources, including Walmart Luminate/Scintilla, Circana, NielsenIQ, or similar platforms, to generate insights and inform business decisions.
Strong financial acumen, analytical capabilities, and experience managing trade investments and business planning processes.
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to lead across a highly matrixed organization.

title: Business Manager
description:
Overview
MCAPS-Core accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.
The Customer & Commercial Success (CCS) organization, an organization within MCAPS-Core, is the connected engine that turns Microsoft’s commercial strategy into execution at scale — making it simpler and faster for the field to win for every customer, in every segment, region, and role. The organization brings together planning, landing, execution excellence, services portfolio and delivery, and field activation across ATU, STU, and CSU to accelerate customer value, drive growth, and strengthen the end-to-end experience across every customer moment.
Within C&CS, the Global Customer Experience (GCX) organization empowers Microsoft to deliver easy and personalized experiences for every customer, every time. Our bold ambition is to see Microsoft recognized as the CX leader across industries. Join us today to be at the forefront of CX strategy, innovation, and to deliver business value through prioritized CX improvements and customer obsessed culture at scale!
Enable GCX to operate as one connected, high-performing organization by leading the rhythm of business, executive and employee communications, and culture. This role turns leadership priorities into clear decisions and an employee experience that strengthens customer impact. The Business Manager is a senior individual contributor and trusted advisor to the Vice President of Global Customer Experience and the GCX Leadership Team. The role connects strategy to execution across a global organization, creating the operating discipline, communication clarity, and culture needed to deliver easy, personalized experiences for every customer, every time. Success depends on leading through influence, building strong cross-functional partnerships, and orchestrating work across leaders, business managers, communications partners, finance, human resources, and program teams.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
1. Business management and rhythm of business
•    Own and continuously improve the GCX rhythm of business, including leadership team meetings, senior leader community and people manager meetings, and organizational cadences (e.g. Townhall, Ask Us Anything, etc.)
•    Partner with the Vice President and leadership team to shape agendas, frame decisions, prepare executive materials, capture decisions, and drive follow-through on commitments.
•    Translate priorities into clear workbacks, owners, milestones, success measures, and escalation paths. Maintain visibility to progress, risks, interdependencies, and decisions needed.
•    Use data and business insights to identify operating gaps, recommend improvements, and increase the speed, quality, and accountability of execution.
•    Coordinate high-priority, cross-team initiatives and time-sensitive responses where clear ownership and orchestration are essential.
2. Executive and organizational communications
•    Lead the GCX communications strategy and editorial calendar across executive, leadership, employee, and organizational channels.
•    Draft and shape clear, audience-centered communications for organizational announcements, leadership updates, town halls, business reviews, and moments of change.
•    Turn complex strategy, performance, and organizational information into simple narratives, messages, and materials that help employees understand what matters and what action to take.
•    Create consistent feedback and listening mechanisms to assess message reach, understanding, employee sentiment, and opportunities to improve communication effectiveness.
•    Partner closely with communications teams and subject matter experts to ensure messaging is accurate, timely, coordinated, and aligned across audiences.
3. Culture and employee experience
•    Own the GCX culture and employee experience plan, translating Microsoft culture attributes and GCX priorities into practical experiences, leadership habits, and ways of working.
•    Partner with leaders and employee communities to strengthen connection, inclusion, recognition, learning, and engagement across a globally distributed organization.
•    Shape culture programs, team forums, recognition moments, employee listening follow-through, and change experiences that build trust and reinforce accountability.
•    Use employee feedback and organizational signals to identify themes, recommend actions, and track whether interventions are improving the employee experience.
•    Help leaders communicate and model expectations consistently, especially during periods of organizational change or ambiguity.
4. Leadership team enablement and special projects
•    Serve as an integrator across the GCX Leadership Team, surfacing connections, gaps, trade-offs, and opportunities that may not be visible within individual functions.
•    Anticipate the Vice President’s and leadership team’s needs, bringing structured recommendations rather than only reporting issues.
•    Lead special projects that require discretion, sound judgment, rapid synthesis, and cross-boundary coordination.
•    Handle sensitive business and organizational information with appropriate confidentiality.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 8+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Master's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 12+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles OR Bachelor's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 15+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles OR equivalent experience.
Experience leading complex, cross-functional work from definition through execution in a large, global organization.
Demonstrated ability to create executive-ready communications and turn complex information into clear decisions, narratives, and actions.
Experience designing and running leadership or business rhythms, including agendas, decision tracking, governance, and follow-through.
Proficient written and verbal communication skills.
Experience supporting a senior executive or leadership team as a business manager, chief of staff partner, communications lead, or senior program manager.
Experience leading culture, employee engagement, change management, or organizational effectiveness initiatives.
Business judgment and analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to distinguish signal from noise and recommend a practical path forward.
Ability to influence without authority, build trust across organizational boundaries, and create alignment among leaders with different perspectives.
Exceptional planning and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines.

High discretion, integrity, and sound judgment when managing sensitive information.

description:
Overview
What our team offers
The Cloud and AI Platforms Monetization (“CAPM”) organization is a big picture team at our core that encourages a diverse and inclusive culture. We are respectful, collaborative, honest, accountable, and caring. Employees on the team can expect to have opportunities to grow their own experience and career while shaping the future of the Azure business with data-informed strategies.
We are growth strategists who monetize product value and improve the buying experience for customers to drive business growth and profitability for Microsoft. The CAPM team enables the Microsoft mission by creating durable profit growth through high-impact monetization strategies, packaging, and pricing.
Enhancing our team culture and team experience is a top priority for our leadership, managers, and team more broadly. Our aspire-to team culture is one with cultural attributes encompassing transparency, growth and development, connection, and productivity and balance, all anchored on promoting diversity and inclusion.
What I will do for you as your manager
Champion your success with the team and with leadership.
Give you the resources and support to succeed and grow your career as a business planner.
Provide opportunities to gain new experiences and build on your strengths.
Support who you are as your authentic self.
Make your career development a consistent priority.
Role Overview and how you can make an impact
As the Business Planner, Azure Container Services and Developer Innovation , you will play a critical role in shaping how Microsoft monetizes and grows some of Azure’s most important container, developer, and emerging AI services.
AI agents are moving from pilot to production, and they need a secure, scalable place to run. On Azure, that place is increasingly containers. This role puts you at the center of that shift: you will shape the business model for the container services that form the foundation for enterprise AI, and you will incubate new products from a blank page.
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is Azure's managed Kubernetes platform, widely adopted by enterprises to run applications at scale, and it is increasingly central to how organizations run AI workloads. Together with Azure Container Instances (ACI), our serverless container service, it gives customers flexible and secure ways to run modern and AI applications on Azure. AKS Edge extends the same Kubernetes experience to edge and on-premises environments, supporting our hybrid strategy for enterprise customers.
You will own planning, pricing, and packaging across AKS Edge, ACI, and Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), a fully managed OpenShift application platform for enterprises modernizing on Kubernetes. The portfolio spans the edge, serverless, and enterprise modernization, giving you a broad portfolio with a clear role in how AI and traditional workloads run on Azure.
You will also lead Azure App Testing, Microsoft's unified testing platform that brings Load Testing, Playwright Testing, and other testing services together under one brand, spanning performance and functional testing. It is a high-growth, developer-centric market, with the global software testing market projected to exceed $500B by 2033, and you will shape pricing, packaging, and adoption to position Azure as the go-to platform for AI and intelligent application quality. Alongside it, you will incubate early-stage, emerging products, where you define the business model from concept to launch and decide what to scale, pivot, or stop.
In this role, you'll convert product roadmap into durable business outcomes by defining monetization strategy, shaping business models, and driving pricing and packaging decisions that deepen product-market fit. You'll contribute to simplifying the customer experience, designing adoption motions, and turning customer signals into clear business and commercial choices. Your work will shape how developers and enterprises adopt and scale AI applications and agents on Azure and in hybrid deployments.
Our team is customer-focused and inclusive, values collaboration and data-driven problem solving, and works across partner teams to define and execute business models and monetization strategies that drive long-term growth. You will partner directly with engineering, product, finance, marketing, sales, and pricing operations, while running an established portfolio and building what comes next.
If you thrive in strategic, cross-functional environments and want to shape both established container services and early-stage bets, this Business Planner, Azure Container Services and Developer Innovation role is a uniquely visible opportunity to define how modern and AI applications are built, tested, and run on Azure.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
As a Business Planner, Azure Container Services, Developer Innovation & Incubations , you can expect to learn from the following activities:
Lead and evolve the monetization strategy for Container Services such as Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), Azure Container Instances (ACI), and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Edge, including pricing, packaging, and revenue growth.
Own the business model for Azure App Testing, from adoption and trial design to pricing and packaging.
Build business models for incubation products from concept to launch.
Bring a quantitative perspective to support your recommendations (i.e. bring data to bear).
Identify pricing and licensing optimization opportunities by interacting closely with partners, sellers, and customers.
Create business model proposals, present them to senior leadership, and drive cross-functional alignment.
Collaborate with pricing operations (i.e. Commerce and Ops) to implement business models and pricing.
Drive revenue growth and track portfolio health across container services and emerging products.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Computer Science, Economics, Business, or related field AND 2+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Computer Science, Economics, Business, or related field AND 5+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience OR Master's Degree in Business Administration (MBA), or related field AND 3+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience
OR equivalent experience.
Track record of working across diverse stakeholders to define and execute strategic initiatives with passion, precision, and excellence.
Analytical problem-solving skills and ability to synthesize data from multiple sources to drive data-driven decisions.
Sound business judgement leveraging strong strategic thinking complemented with a bias for action and execution/operational excellence.
Great communication and leadership skills to drive projects and build executive buy-in and support for key projects.
Comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to build structure for early-stage products.

title: Client Delivery Partner (CDP) - Oil & Gas Industry
description:
Overview
Industry Solutions Delivery (ISD) is a global organization of more than 6,000 strategic sellers, industry experts, engineers, architects, consultants, and delivery professionals. We work side by side with the world’s most influential companies to deliver Microsoft technology and accelerate their digital transformation journeys. Our team values diverse perspectives and encourages everyone to be their authentic self. Join us to help create innovations that make a global impact.
As a Client Delivery Partner (CDP) – Oil & Gas Industry , you are the executive accountable to Microsoft’s largest customers, many of them Fortune 500 and global enterprises, for the transformation programs we shape and deliver together. You build direct, trusted relationships with C-suite technology leaders, especially the CIO, CTO, and CISO, alongside business executives such as the COO. Working shoulder to shoulder with Microsoft account teams, you co-create the solutions and deals that move these customers forward, then stand behind them as the executive accountable for delivering the promised outcomes.
This is an executive-level deal-shaping and delivery leadership role. It is not a project management role. You partner with your Microsoft account team counterparts, including Account Team Unit (ATU) account executives, Specialist Team Unit (STU) solution and technical specialists, Industry Advisors, and Solution Sales Professionals (SSPs), to originate, shape, scope, and close opportunities. That work spans deal shaping, solution architecture direction, commercial structuring, estimates, statements of work (SOWs), risk and deal reviews, and executive orals.
Once an engagement is sold, your accountability is executive oversight. You lead and coach the program managers and delivery leaders who run each engagement, serve as a part-time executive sponsor and escalation point, and own the executive relationship and governance through steering committees and executive business reviews. You are accountable for outcomes, customer satisfaction, financial health, and expansion, but you are not involved in day-to-day project management, status tracking, or task-level execution. The role typically spans a portfolio of engagements simultaneously.
The job location for this role is Houston, Texas with up to 4 days in-office/with the customer onsite.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our culture embraces a growth mindset, inspires excellence, and encourages teams and leaders to bring their best each day. Together, we create innovations that impact billions of people around the world, and you can help us deliver on that mission.

Shape and win transformational deals with the account team
Partner with ATU account executives, STU solution and technical specialists, Industry Advisors, and SSPs to originate, shape, and close large, multi-year services opportunities.
Lead deal shaping end to end: frame the customer’s business problem, set solution architecture direction, and define scope, approach, and success measures.
Own the commercial structure of each deal, including estimates, pricing approach, fixed-fee and outcome-based models, and statements of work.
Lead risk and deal reviews so that every engagement is set up to deliver predictable value and healthy margin.

Partner with Microsoft executives to align industry insight, technology strategy, and customer business outcomes.

Lead and coach the program managers and delivery leaders who own day-to-day execution, setting clear expectations for quality, outcomes, and customer experience.
Serve as part-time executive sponsor and escalation point across a portfolio of concurrent engagements, stepping in decisively when issues require attention.

Hold delivery teams accountable for outcomes, customer satisfaction, and financial health, while leaving project management and task-level execution with them.

Build and grow pipeline with the account team, turning delivered value into follow-on engagements and expanded scope.
Accelerate Microsoft Cloud consumption and adoption by ensuring solutions reach production and deliver measurable business value.

A Microsoft Construction Quality Manager is responsible for governing the quality management system, auditing contractor quality performance, managing NCRs and quality metrics, identifying risks before they impact commissioning or operations, and ensuring data centers are delivered ready to perform—not just ready to complete.
Responsibilities
Core Responsibilities of a Microsoft Construction Quality Manager
1. Drive Construction Quality from Day One
Ensure facilities are built in accordance with design requirements, specifications, and Microsoft quality standards.
Promote a "Right First Time" culture to reduce rework, delays, and operational risks.
2. Audit Contractor Quality Programs
Verify General Contractors are executing their Quality Management System (QMS).
Conduct routine quality audits, inspections, and field observations.
Validate contractor compliance with Division 01 requirements, quality plans, inspection processes, and documentation requirements.
3. Manage NCRs and Quality Issues
Initiate and manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
Ensure corrective actions are developed, implemented, and verified.
Escalate unresolved quality issues to project leadership.
Trend recurring quality problems and drive systemic corrective actions.
4. Quality Management System Ownership
Establish and maintain project quality plans.
Review and align contractor quality plans before mobilization.
Standardize quality processes across projects and campuses.
5. Inspection & Test Planning Governance
Govern Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs).
Define hold points, quality gates, and documentation requirements.
Ensure Installer Verification Checklists (IVCs) and readiness requirements are met before commissioning milestones.
6. Digital Quality Platform Management
Administer quality tracking systems (Nexus/ACMS).
Monitor issue closure timelines and SLA performance.
Produce dashboards and quality metrics for leadership visibility.
7. Field Quality Assurance
Perform field inspections and observations.
Monitor workmanship trends and installation quality.
Verify contractors are following approved procedures and specifications.
Provide early identification of risks that could impact commissioning, IST, or turnover.
8. Readiness and Turnover Support
Support energization and commissioning readiness reviews.
Ensure documentation, inspections, punch lists, and quality issues are appropriately closed prior to turnover.
Partner with Commissioning Managers and Operations to improve startup outcomes.
9. Continuous Improvement
Analyze trends across campuses and metros.
Capture lessons learned.
Recommend process improvements that improve quality performance and reduce recurrence of defects.
10. Contractor Accountability
Hold GCs accountable for their QA/QC responsibilities.
Monitor closure performance and response times.
Reinforce that workmanship quality remains the responsibility of the contractor. Microsoft Quality provides oversight and assurance.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
7+ years experience working on data center projects.
Proficient in data analytics, reporting, and construction management tools such as Power BI, Nexus, Bluebeam, and BIM with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Detail-oriented with strong knowledge of construction specifications, quality standards, and installation compliance requirements.
Experience with continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean, DMAIC, Six Sigma, and change management.
Experience applying structured problem-solving tools such as RCA, FMEA, 8D, and CAPA.
Knowledge of ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems, quality auditing, and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) principles.
Experience developing, implementing, and managing structured quality management systems.
Professional quality certifications preferred, including USACE CQM, OSHA 30, ASQ CQE, CQA, CMQ/OE, Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, or equivalent.
Experience in data center, mission-critical, industrial, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, power, or oil & gas construction environments preferred.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings.
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

title: Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization
description:
Overview
About Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL)
Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL) is a newly formed organization at the core of Microsoft's Business strategy. MSL brings together the teams that decide how Microsoft prices, packages, and monetizes its commercial products, together with the licensing programs and partner agreements that carry that commercial model to market.
The organization was established as Microsoft enters its next phase of AI-driven transformation, when customer expectations and commercial models are shifting faster than ever. MSL's charter is to modernize the commercial engine beneath that shift: evolving legacy licensing constructs toward cloud- and consumption-based models, growing multi-billion-dollar revenue streams, and keeping Microsoft's programs both compliant and competitive across a complex global regulatory landscape.
Role Overview
The Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization leads the modernization of Microsoft's legacy Volume Licensing (VL) programs: the Microsoft Products & Services Agreement (MPSA), Select and Select Plus, and the Open family of programs (Open License, Open Value, and Open Value Subscription). These programs were designed for a perpetual-license, on-premises world. As customer needs shift to cloud and consumption, this role will shape how they evolve alongside Microsoft’s modern commerce motions.
This role owns the strategy to evolve these programs and guide customers and partners toward CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct, while preserving revenue, protecting customers with legitimate perpetual-licensing needs, and minimizing disruption to partners and channels. The successful candidate will operate with significant independence, lead complex cross-group work as an individual contributor, influencing without direct authority across finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field teams, and bring well-framed, data-driven options to senior leadership.
Responsibilities
Strategic Programs You Will Modernize / Key Responsibilities
This role modernizes a set of long-lived, high-revenue programs that are central to Microsoft's shift toward subscription and cloud-based commerce:
Legacy VL Program Strategy and Roadmap
Own the end-to-end strategy for MPSA, Select / Select Plus, and Open Value / Open Value Subscription. This includes building the diagnostic fact base on legacy program growth dynamics and EA-to-legacy migration patterns, evaluating future-state options and ensuring customers with specialized needs  (public sector, regulated procurement, air-gapped, and long-lifecycle scenarios).
Modern Commerce Motion Transition
Design structured migration paths that move legacy VL customers and partners to CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct while preserving customer relationships and revenue. Drive the business requirements for the modern-commerce capabilities this transition depends on, including perpetual-licensing support, indirect resell, and public sector constructs in MCA-E. Lead the opportunity to evolve transactional license sales in favor of subscription, to which MPSA, Select, and Open are major contributors.
Price Optimization and Revenue Yield
Drive pricing and program strategy across the legacy VL portfolio, using pricing, product, and partner levers together to deliver customer value and support the move to modern commerce. Bring the analytical rigor to scenario-plan and quantify the revenue, customer, and partner impact of every pricing and program action before it ships, across commercial, government, education, and non-profit segments.
Program Integrity, Compliance and Regulatory Risk
Keep legacy programs compliant while they remain in market. Partner with legal, risk, and engineering teams to strengthen program integrity while preserving legitimate customer pathways. Navigate anti-competition, transferability, and data-sovereignty considerations across geographies, applying geo-segmented treatment for international markets where appropriate.
Leadership Responsibilities
Lead large, cross-group virtual teams without direct authority, spanning finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field organizations, through a dependency-driven, iterative strategy that keeps workstreams aligned and decisions moving.
Represent the work at leadership levels within and external to the company, bringing well-framed options and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Partner with external partners and internal product, engineering, finance, field, CELA, and partner teams to land changes with minimal market disruption.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Computer Science, Economics, Business, or related field AND 6+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications:
Substantial experience (typically 5+ years) in commercial licensing, volume licensing programs, pricing, or partner-program strategy, with deep subject-matter expertise in Microsoft's volume licensing and modern commerce models (CSP, MCA-E, Web Direct).
Proven command of pricing and business-model strategy, and the analytical discipline to quantify the impact of pricing and program decisions.
Experience leading large-scale program transitions, including customer, partner, and channel change management.
Familiarity with public sector and regulated procurement requirements, and with the legal and regulatory considerations that shape licensing program changes across geographies.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity and influence without authority across finance, commerce, engineering, legal, partner, and sales organizations.
Direct, credible written and verbal communication and the independence to bring well-framed options to senior stakeholders at the company.

The Principal Partner Ecosystem Strategy Lead is a senior strategy role responsible for identifying and advancing high-impact growth opportunities across Microsoft's partner and ISV ecosystem.

They will determine which opportunities warrant investment, develop the strategic hypothesis and business case, and work across Microsoft organizations to validate the opportunity through analysis, customer and partner evidence, and focused pilots.
For opportunities that prove material, this leader will establish the strategy and intervention, mobilize the right cross-functional teams to test it, define measures of success, and ultimately transition proven motions or mechanisms to the appropriate long-term business owner.
This is not a traditional partner management or program management role. It requires strategic judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to create clarity and momentum across complex problems without relying on formal authority or established playbooks.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Connect signals across commercial models, incentives, customer engagement, technical investment, Marketplace, field execution, and partner strategy to identify opportunities that may not be visible within any single organization.
Distinguish between isolated operational friction and systemic constraints that materially affect growth.
Develop clear hypotheses about the business opportunity, affected behavior, potential intervention, and expected impact.

Partner with product management and other business, technical, commercial, and field teams across Microsoft to design focused pilots and experiments.
Establish clear go/no-go criteria and use evidence to refine, scale, redirect, or stop initiatives.
Maintain strategic ownership of the opportunity while drawing on functional experts and execution teams across Microsoft.

Translate validated opportunities into repeatable growth motions, operating mechanisms, commercial approaches, or changes to existing business processes.
Identify where organizational seams, incentives, ownership models, or existing mechanisms inhibit partner-led growth and determine the highest-leverage intervention.
Define how successful interventions can operate through existing Microsoft organizations rather than creating unnecessary parallel structures.
Develop clear ownership, measurement, governance, and transition models for initiatives that prove successful.

Build coalitions across business groups, sales, engineering, commercial, finance, Marketplace, partner, and customer organizations.
Navigate situations in which multiple organizations own portions of a problem but no organization owns the end-to-end opportunity.

Agents increasingly act autonomously over long horizons and have access to tools, files, networks, and credentials. Two problems limit how far they can be trusted: they fail in ways that aggregate benchmark scores hide, and they can be manipulated by adversarial inputs. This Research Internship offers two research directions, with Research Interns focusing on one based on their expertise and interests:
Failure-driven self-improvement:  improve long-horizon agents by diagnosing failure modes in their trajectories and synthesizing targeted post-training data that closes specific capability gaps.
Agent security:  develop technologies that make existing agentic systems more secure, including sandboxing, agent permissions, and defenses against novel agent attacks.

description:
Overview
We are looking for a multidisciplinary AIX Creative Technologist who blends the instincts of a designer, the creative vision of a storyteller, and the technical fluency of a creative engineer. Embedded within the Creative Studio, you will help imagine and shape the future of Copilot and AI experiences by exploring new product ideas, features, interactions, and embodied AI characters, while building working prototypes that bring those possibilities to life.
This role brings together product design, interaction design, animation, AI, storytelling, and software development. You will explore emerging technologies, experiment with new forms of human–AI interaction, and develop prototypes, tools, and reusable systems that help move ideas from early exploration toward real product experiences.
The ideal candidate is as comfortable imagining new product possibilities and crafting intuitive, expressive experiences as writing code, connecting systems, and debugging prototypes. You should bring deep expertise in at least one discipline and a demonstrated ability to bridge creative thinking and technical execution.
The future of Copilot and AI must be experienced, not just imagined. From entirely new product ideas, features, and interactions to embodied AI characters and how they move, speak, behave, and respond, the most compelling possibilities come to life through tangible, interactive experiences that people can see, feel, and explore.
You will help build the Creative Studio’s ability to imagine, prototype, validate, and bring these ideas to life—connecting creative strategy, design, storytelling, and emerging technologies to new product possibilities, strengthening shared technical capabilities, and bridging the gap between creative vision and implementation.
Responsibilities
Develop and prototype future AI experiences. Translate blue-sky Copilot and AI product ideas, narratives, and creative concepts into compelling UI explorations, UX flows, interactive demos, and working prototypes that advance the product experience, brand, identity, and creative vision.
Design embodied AI characters and experiences. Shape character identity, visual language, motion, expression, personality, and behavior across products and platforms, including onboarding, customization, voice, and feedback systems that make AI experiences intuitive, expressive, and trustworthy.
Build interactive, real-time systems. Develop, debug, and optimize character animation, input, and response systems, connecting UI frameworks such as React, real-time rendering technologies such as Babylon.js, and AI services into cohesive, performant experiences across platforms, including mobile.
Prototype with AI agents and emerging technologies. Experiment with conversational, multimodal, generative, and multi-agent systems, integrating models, tools, and services to coordinate actions, manage state, and explore new ways people interact with AI.
Bridge creative vision and engineering execution. Build everything from lightweight experiments to production-minded prototypes, working within established code architectures and engineering frameworks to develop maintainable, reusable components and evaluate technical feasibility.
Collaborate, validate, and scale ideas. Partner with Research, Design, Product, and Engineering to test tension, trust, and emotional response, refine concepts, and develop shared tools, workflows, and design patterns that accelerate creative exploration and implementation across the studio.

Experience optimizing performance across platforms, particularly mobile, balancing visual quality, rendering cost, memory, loading times, and responsiveness.

Hands-on experience working with AI agents, including integrating models, tools, and services into interactive, user-facing experiences.
A track record of developing or shipping experiences using emerging technologies such as real-time 3D, games, generative AI, VR, or AR.

An understanding of human-centered design and how timing, feedback, personality, and behavior influence clarity, usability, and trust.
Experience developing enterprise or consumer software products, with an appreciation for accessibility, reliability, maintainability, and long-term usability beyond one-off demos or entertainment experiences.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across Creative, Research, Product, and Engineering to develop, evaluate, and advance ideas from early exploration toward implementation.

This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other CE Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometimes minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Other
Embodies our  culture  and  values .

Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Develops a comprehensive understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

We are seeking a Senior Firmware Engineer with experience with firmware development and Rust experience to develop and debug shared firmware components, support platform bring-up, and improve firmware reliability, security, and maintainability.

Develop reusable firmware frameworks, libraries, hardware abstraction layers, device drivers, and common services, with attention to memory management, resource constraints, reliability, and performance.

Collaborate with silicon, hardware, platform, validation, and software engineering teams to define requirements, document interfaces, resolve technical issues, and deliver reusable firmware across programs.

Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.   In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.    Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties

Customer Service

Engages with internal and external stakeholders, building relationships with vendors and providing oversight, to manage issues as they arise. Collaborates with the IAM Standard team and Engineering team to execute and refine pilot processes, tools, or feature enhancements.

Manages schedule of data bearing devices (DBD) destruction or shredding in partnership with security and senior leadership. Acts as a comprehensive resource for the decommissioning process to ensure customer security is maintained, performing data bearing devices (DBD) destruction as necessary. Handles any escalations. Assists with security investigations, supporting data bearing devices (DBD) reconciliations with review of current documentation and extensive back tracking of ticket details. Coordinates with and oversees any third-party vendors who perform data bearing devices (DBD) destruction as necessary. Ensures team decommissions servers, maintaining compliance and meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs), overseeing documentation of actions taken against a decommissioning workflow.
Fleet Management Serve as primary liaison for overseeing the fleet management program, maintenance vendors and equipment check-in and check-out process. Define numbers of vehicles needed and what type of vehicles & equipment (e.g. Ford Pick, Box Truck, Esco Sport, etc.) with the Vehicle and Fleet PM, identifying and reporting gaps within the fleet to leadership. Oversee scheduled and preventative maintenance via in-house and vendor provided service. Manage, route, and fulfill transportation requests for Information Technology, Critical Environment, and Logistics, and other supported teams. Audits vehicles and fleet resources, ensuring vehicles are present in the correct location with assigned resources (e.g., gas card, gas card PIN).
