Schedules inbound and outbound logistics of both internal and external services. Communicates directly with customers, stakeholders, vendors, (e.g., landlords) in regard to scheduling both inbound and outbound deliveries. Coordinates with external stakeholders including third-party warehouses, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) vendors, and suppliers as necessary to facilitate inbound and outbound deliveries. Conducts follow-ups on items logged within Intelligence Communication Manager (iCM), validating issues, and deals with the escalated issues. Supports creating more efficient receiving routes, moving manual communication and information sharing to automated processes, where possible.
IT Inventory Management Ensures teams maintain and perform steps required to keep the inventory balance accurate. Plans, forecasts, and develops strategies for space optimization, including decommissioning and retention, driving identification of opportunities to improve inventory to address space constraints and ensuring deprecated materials are not stagnant. Prioritizes ticketing queues, works to resolve escalations, and clears blocking issues to enable continued delivery of Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) activities.
Operational Excellence Serves as subject matter expert and models compliance to less experienced team members. Seeks out opportunities to contribute to workstreams and toward greater simplification and automation, improving results of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) against Objective Key Results (OKRs). Conducts root cause analysis and identifies training gaps for potential escalations. Facilitates and pilots environmental sustainability and zero waste initiatives. Completes required security and data management training and complies with security and data management procedures/policies. Conducts training for relevant site-specific procedures and tools (e.g., forklift, pallet jacks, technician on-hand processes, inventory maintenance software, RMA portals, Rack Movement).
Procurement Creates execution plans with the goal to improve satisfaction and performance within an area or organization-level group. Identifies and resolves delivery and execution road blocks, serving as point of contact for arising issues and unblocking critical paths to continue business continuity. Learns different elements of different suppliers, including what parts to order and what supplier(s) to engage with. Gathers data related to POs and provides to direct management. Assists senior leadership with escalated procurement issues. Performs quality control for purchase order and escalations with vendors. Audits on-site supplies and deployment consumables.

Manages and coordinates any escalated task risks and reported issues, establishing safety standard operating procedures for new equipment (e.g., server rack tugs, electric pallet jacks, forklifts). Trains employees on safe and effective equipment and inventory moving. Ensures team and 3rd party vendors are in compliance with Microsoft Corporation safety standards Procures, audits, and reviews personal protective equipment (PPE), leading by example of all safety standards. Presents Identity and Access Management (IAM) metrics to senior leaders. Supervises rack movement, observing to ensure compliance with safety protocols and training others on devices and tools used in rack movement. Oversees handling and storage of hazardous materials and chemicals, developing plans to address unsafe materials out of containment and ensuring preparedness of others, and acting as a point of escalation.

Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

title: Senior Security Operations Engineer
description:
Overview
Team overview
Every cloud depends on a small set of foundational services that almost everything else trusts. Together they form the cloud's Trusted Computing Base (TCB): the services where a small gap can have an outsized blast radius across the cloud and the customers who depend on it.
These are Microsoft's crown jewels, and protecting them is urgent: sophisticated attackers target exactly these kinds of services, and AI is making it faster to find and exploit weaknesses. Securing them is always top of mind for senior leadership, it comes first when we prioritize risk reduction, and the controls we prove here set the paved path for production services across the company.
The TCB Core Security Engineering team in IAM Protect, part of Microsoft's CISO organization, leads this work. We take a data-driven, attack-path view of risk, modeling the trust relationships between services to understand blast radius and focus our effort where it reduces the most risk. We are a technically deep security that operates horizontally across Microsoft. Our strategy is simple to state and hard to do: isolate these services from the rest of the cloud, minimize what has to be trusted, and defend what remains with layered controls.
Role overview
We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer who pairs a deep understanding of how cloud services and platforms are actually constructed with the security instincts to see where they can be broken. You will identify new risks to our crown jewel services, model them with our attack-path and risk data, develop the policies and security controls that close them, and partner with leaders and service owners across Microsoft to drive those controls to adoption until the exposure is measurably gone. Every attack path you shut down is one no attacker can use against Microsoft's cloud or its customers.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Responsibilities
•    Identify and analyze risk across our most critical cloud services. Look for unintended trust and access paths into them, such as excessive privilege, credential exposure and unnecessary access between services, and turn findings into clear, prioritized risk statements.
•    Model risk with data. Work with service owners and architects to understand how their services are built, represent trust relationships accurately, and use attack-path analysis to quantify blast radius and decide which paths to remove first.
•    Develop security policies and controls that are enforceable by default rather than dependent on reviews, such as isolation boundaries, least privilege and hardening standards, each with a clear scope, safe rollout, exception handling and validation telemetry.
•    Drive risk burn-down to closure. Lead campaigns with service owners and engineering leaders across Microsoft, set targets, track progress with data, unblock teams, manage exceptions with discipline and report measurable risk reduction to senior leadership.
•    Leverage AI to automate workflows, improve efficiency, and streamline your work.
•    Govern and defend the boundary around these services. Define and run the mechanisms that keep the set of critical services small and well isolated, and partner with detection, incident response and eviction teams so we can assume breach and still contain an attacker quickly.
•    Turn incidents and red team findings into durable protection by converting the lessons into risk models, policies and controls, so the same path cannot be used twice.
•    Scale your impact with data and automation: build KQL queries, datasets, dashboards and AI-assisted tooling that make risk discovery, prioritization and campaign tracking faster.
•    Produce crisp technical artifacts, including risk write-ups, control specifications, troubleshooting guides and leadership updates that unblock execution.
Qualifications

Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR equivalent experience. Additional or preferred qualifications
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 6+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 8+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection
OR equivalent experience.
•    6+ years of experience in cloud security engineering, security architecture, offensive security or incident response in a hyperscale or large enterprise environment.
•    Deep knowledge of how cloud services are constructed: identity and token issuance (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and service-to-service authentication), service principals and managed identities, PKI and certificate lifecycle, secret and key management, role-based access and control-plane authorization, build and release pipelines, and network segmentation.

The AI Deployment Manager (ADM) team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.

By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens meaningful adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.

The AI Deployment Manager, Builder role is a specialist post-sales technical enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. You will design and deliver technical learning experiences covering OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, evaluations, and related platform capabilities. You will work with engineers, AI and platform teams, administrators, security stakeholders, product leaders, and executive sponsors.

This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from hands-on builders to executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 - Lead customer training and enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.

 - Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when conveying the value of technical concepts clearly to senior and executive-level audiences.

 - Strong technical depth across software engineering, the software development lifecycle, and APIs, with a practical understanding of how AI systems are built, evaluated, and operated in production, including RAG, evaluation strategies, agentic systems and key tradeoffs.

 - Proven experience leading structured technical trainings, such as API bootcamps, workshops, or enablement sessions, with the ability to design learning journeys, handle live questions, and reason through problems in real time.

 - Strong ability to connect technical features and capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity, efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

 - Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help others, and a desire to pick up whatever knowledge you're missing to make both your team and our customers succeed.

title: Deal Operations, AMER
description:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across the Americas (AMER) by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for AMER account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for AMER account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

 - Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

 - Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

 - Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

 - Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

 - Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

 - Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

 - Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

 - Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

 - Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

 - Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

 - Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

 - Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

 - Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

 - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

description:
ABOUT THIS TEAM

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We stay close enough to the business to understand how it works and focus our time on the decisions that benefit most from our judgment, context, and influence.

We work with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Senior HR Business Partner supporting Tech, you’ll partner with leaders in engineering, product, and other technical teams as they build and scale their organizations. You’ll get close enough to the work to understand what’s slowing teams down, then help leaders make decisions about structure, talent, and how teams work together as technical priorities evolve.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. You’ll advise senior leaders on complex decisions and work directly with managers to make those decisions stick.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Translate technical priorities into org and talent decisions. Help leaders decide what capabilities to build, how to structure teams, and where ownership needs to sit.

 - Diagnose what’s getting in the way of team performance. Use data and input from the people doing the work to separate structural issues from problems with roles, priorities, or how teams work together.

 - Develop technical leaders. Coach managers through performance, growth, and succession decisions, and help them set clear expectations for both people managers and individual contributors.

 - Lead change as technical priorities shift. Help leaders think through the impact of reorganizations or changes in ownership and communicate decisions clearly to the teams affected.

 - Build People practices that work for technical teams. Partner with fellow HRBPs and People specialists to adapt performance, development, and talent processes without adding unnecessary overhead.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in a high-growth or complex environment.

 - Experience partnering with engineering, product, or other technical organizations, and curiosity about how technical teams make decisions and deliver work.

 - A track record of helping technical leaders navigate org design, workforce planning, or talent decisions as teams grow or priorities change.

 - Skill in coaching senior leaders and managers, including the ability to challenge a decision constructively and maintain trust.

 - Sound judgment under pressure and the ability to act on incomplete information while staying open to new evidence.

 - Discretion, fairness, and sound judgment when the stakes are high.


WORKPLACE & LOCATION

This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office and is not available remotely. We offer relocation support to new employees. Our hybrid model is three days in the office per week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

OpenAI’s in-house Creative Team is looking for a Motion Design Producer to help shape and scale how our brand comes to life through motion design across every touchpoint — from identity systems and campaigns to product, web, and comms work.

You’ll partner closely with our Brand Identity & Brand Design leadership to manage intake, resourcing, timelines, and creative workflows — ensuring design projects move seamlessly from concept to delivery. You’ll serve as the operational backbone of the design practice, building clarity and momentum across a growing cross-functional team. As Motion Design is a shared function in Creative Design, you will also partner closely with other production functional ecosystems to deliver motion design support.

This is a highly collaborative role that requires both strategic oversight and hands-on execution. You’ll be a key connector across Marketing, Product, Comms, and Web — driving alignment, enabling great design, and creating the systems that keep our creative work consistent, efficient, and impactful.

 - Elevate Systems & Process: Design and implement operational frameworks that enable the design team to scale effectively — from creative reviews and feedback loops to asset tracking and tool optimization.

 - Uphold Craft & Consistency: Partner with the Brand Identity and Brand Design team to ensure design work is cohesive, high-quality, and reflective of OpenAI’s evolving visual identity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 8+ years of experience in design production, brand operations, or creative program management within an in-house team or agency environment.

 - Are fluent in the design process — from concept and iteration through production and delivery — and can anticipate what a creative team needs to succeed. Should be experienced in full identity explorations and production needs.

title: Researcher, Frontier Robustness
description:
About the Team

The Frontier Robustness team advances the science of securing frontier AI systems. We develop new methods to keep increasingly capable models contained, observable, and under human control, focusing on the sandboxes, shared research infrastructure, and protective systems used during model development and evaluation.

We use our most capable models to discover and combine weaknesses across the security stack, studying how they might escape containment, communicate through unauthorized channels, or evade monitoring. We turn these findings into new defenses and test whether protections hold as models, environments, and attack strategies change.



About the Role

We are looking for a researcher to develop and test new methods for securing frontier AI systems. You will investigate open-ended questions about model behavior, containment, and safeguards—designing experiments, building evaluations, and developing defenses where established approaches may be insufficient. You will work closely with the Security organization to define the problems and translate research findings into practical protections.

You will take research from an initial question and threat model through experiment design, reproducible findings, and tested defenses. You will write code, build tools and prototypes, and work closely with researchers and infrastructure owners to turn new ideas into safeguards that work in practice. This requires sound security judgment, comfort with uncertainty, and the ability to devise solutions to problems without established answers. This role is based in San Francisco.



In this role, you will:

 - Design and run experiments using frontier models and hands-on security techniques to discover failure modes in sandboxes, research infrastructure, and the services models can reach. Reproduce vulnerabilities and assess their impact.

 - Develop threat models and novel adversarial tests for attacks that cross multiple security boundaries, including sandbox escapes, unauthorized communication between agents, and access to sensitive data or systems through shared services.

 - Invent, prototype, and evaluate defenses that strengthen isolation and limit the impact of a compromised boundary. Study agent permissions and tool configurations to identify excessive access and build layered protections with infrastructure owners.

 - Develop and red-team model-based safeguards and monitors of model reasoning and actions. Investigate evasion, test new monitoring techniques, and measure when protections detect or prevent unsafe behavior.

 - Develop automated adversarial tests and repeatable evaluations to measure progress as model capabilities, configurations, and attack strategies change. Assess whether defenses generalize to new attacks, verify fixes, and identify regressions.

 - Partner across Research, Security, and infrastructure teams, including Agent Security, to prioritize risks and turn findings into deployed improvements while accounting for performance and researcher workflows.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on experience conducting research with large language models, including designing and running experiments and evaluating model behavior.

 - Can turn an open-ended question into a clear hypothesis, build reproducible experiments at scale, and use the results to develop or improve a method.

 - Can design rigorous evaluations, investigate unexpected results, and test whether findings hold across different models, environments, and attack strategies.

 - Write and debug code independently, build research tools and prototypes, and carry ideas through experimentation.

 - Bring practical security experience relevant to this work, such as sandboxing, vulnerability research, adversarial testing, or detection and monitoring.

 - Work effectively with Security and infrastructure partners to develop threat models, interpret findings, and turn promising research into deployed safeguards.

About the Team

The Agent Identity team builds the foundational identity infrastructure that enables AI agents to securely act on behalf of users and organizations. We develop the systems that allow agents to establish their identity, demonstrate whose authority they are operating under, and securely access resources across applications and environments.

Our team owns agent identity and delegation, authentication and authorization, credential lifecycle management, revocation, and integrations with external platforms. We also build Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling OpenAI to serve as an identity provider across a growing ecosystem of applications.

As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, our work is foundational to how users, organizations, and developers establish trust in agentic systems.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced software engineers to design and build the identity infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents across OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and Codex.

You will tackle complex, largely unsolved engineering challenges at the intersection of identity, security, distributed systems, and agent infrastructure. You’ll help define how agents authenticate across environments, how users securely delegate authority to agents, and how agents interact with external applications and services.

This is an opportunity to shape foundational technical primitives at OpenAI while helping influence how the broader industry approaches identity in an increasingly agent-driven world.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build foundational agent identity primitives, including agent authentication, delegated authorization, and credential lifecycle management.

 - Develop secure mechanisms that enable agents to act on behalf of users and organizations across internal and external systems.

 - Architect authentication and authorization flows for connectors, third-party applications, and cloud-based agent execution environments.

 - Build and evolve Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling secure identity federation and interoperability across the broader application ecosystem.

 - Design highly scalable, reliable, and secure distributed systems that support credential issuance, rotation, revocation, and access enforcement.

 - Partner closely with engineering, product, security, and external platform teams to solve emerging identity challenges and help shape industry standards.

 - Drive technical direction and own complex initiatives from initial architecture through production deployment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or business-critical backend infrastructure.

 - Have deep technical experience in identity and access management, workload identity, identity providers, authentication, authorization, or credential lifecycle management.

 - Alternatively, have experience building cloud-based AI agents, agent execution environments, browser-based automation, or connector infrastructure, with firsthand exposure to identity and authentication challenges.

 - Have familiarity with identity and authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, or related emerging standards.

title: Software Engineer, Presence
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production.

Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email.

One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users.

Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

 


WHAT WE WORK ON

 - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic.

 - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies.

 - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes.

 - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments.

The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/

We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world.

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

Working with cross-functional teams, you will translate scientific advances into meaningful health insights for millions of Oura members.
What You Will Do:
Develop and validate signal processing and machine learning algorithms that enable new health sensing capabilities in future Oura products.
Own exploratory research, design experiments to address key scientific and technical uncertainties, and build proof-of-concept capabilities to establish which sensing concepts are worth advancing.
Design and support internal and external data collection studies to develop, benchmark, and validate new biomarkers and algorithms.
Analyze signals from hardware and firmware prototypes, investigate noise sources and measurement limitations, and recommend improvements to sensing quality and reliability.
Work closely with engineering, product, and design teams across locations to define sensing requirements, evaluate technical trade-offs, and advance promising concepts through product development.
Document and present scientific findings and algorithm performance to technical and nontechnical audiences, with actionable recommendations that guide research priorities and product decisions.
This role is hybrid, with at least three days in office at either our Carmel Mountain location in San Diego (preferred) or San Francisco office.
What you'll bring
A PhD with 3+ years of relevant work experience, or an MSc with 5+ years, in biomedical engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, neural engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of hands-on Python programming experience, with strong coding skills and experience using Git and participating in code reviews.

Drive adoption of self-service reporting by Hardware Engineering, Quality, and Product partners using a variety of analytics tools and creating clear documentation to reduce one-off reporting and free up analyst time for analysis.

Experience with modern BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Databricks SQL Dashboards, Power BI) and a clear point of view on when each is the right fit.

A defining responsibility of this position will be helping Quince transition into a significantly larger, more complex headquarters building in San Francisco. The Director will partner with internal leadership, the relocation project manager, architects, contractors, and service providers to ensure the new headquarters is fully operational, exceptionally maintained, and equipped to support the company's continued growth.  The role will
Following the relocation, this leader will oversee all aspects of headquarters facilities operations, including building systems, maintenance, workplace services, security coordination, vendor management, budgets, sample and fabric library operations, and ongoing improvements.

Partner with the relocation project manager, architects, construction teams, designers, IT, Security, and executive leadership to ensure a successful transition.
Develop and execute a comprehensive facilities operational-readiness plan for the new headquarters.
Oversee building systems commissioning, operational testing, inspections, and facilities handover.
Establish required maintenance programs, vendor contracts, workplace services, and operating procedures prior to occupancy.
Ensure the new headquarters supports a significantly larger employee population and more complex workplace services.
Coordinate the readiness of conference facilities, employee amenities, shared spaces, and sample and fabric library areas.
Develop staffing plans, operating budgets, and service standards appropriate for the new facility.
Lead post-occupancy stabilization and establish a scalable facilities operating model.

Own day-to-day facilities operations, ensuring a safe, clean, functional, and professionally maintained workplace.
Oversee HVAC, electrical, plumbing, lighting, elevators, building management systems, and other critical infrastructure.
Develop preventive and predictive maintenance programs to maximize reliability and minimize disruptions.
Manage janitorial services, repairs, waste management, pest control, and general building maintenance.
Establish a centralized work-order management system with defined service-level expectations.
Ensure facilities issues are resolved with urgency and accountability.

Oversee conference rooms, meeting facilities, kitchens, breakrooms, common areas, and employee amenities.
Manage food, beverage, coffee, snack, and related workplace service programs as applicable.
Partner with IT to ensure meeting spaces and audiovisual systems remain functional.
Support company meetings, leadership events, and headquarters activities.
Continuously improve employee workplace experience through responsive service and thoughtful facilities management.

Directly manage and develop a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators responsible for the organization, tracking, storage, and movement of product samples and fabric materials.
Establish and enforce standardized procedures for sample intake, labeling, cataloging, storage, checkout, transfers, and disposition.
Maintain highly accurate sample and fabric inventories, ensuring materials are properly identified, recorded, and readily accessible.
Implement inventory control systems and periodic physical audits to maintain sample inventory accuracy above 95% .
Partner with Merchandising, Design, Product Development, and other stakeholders to ensure samples and fabrics are available when needed.
Establish clear accountability for missing, misplaced, damaged, or incorrectly cataloged samples.
Optimize library layouts, storage capacity, organization, and retrieval processes within the new headquarters.
Oversee the relocation and accurate reconciliation of existing sample and fabric inventories into the new facility.
Develop KPIs and reporting for sample accuracy, retrieval efficiency, inventory discrepancies, and library service levels.
Continuously improve sample handling processes to reduce loss, improve accessibility, and increase operational efficiency.

Develop and manage annual headquarters facilities operating budgets and capital expenditure plans.
Establish financial models and operating budgets for the larger headquarters facility.
Maintain financial controls over utilities, maintenance, contracted services, workplace amenities, and capital projects.
Identify cost efficiencies without compromising workplace quality or operational reliability.
Negotiate competitive vendor agreements and monitor performance.
Develop multiyear capital maintenance and infrastructure replacement plans.
Provide regular financial reporting, forecasts, and variance analyses.

Select, negotiate, and manage third-party facilities service providers.
Establish measurable service-level agreements and performance expectations.
Conduct vendor performance reviews and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Ensure contractors comply with safety, insurance, regulatory, and company requirements.
Maintain productive relationships with landlords, property management, building engineers, and service providers.

Ensure compliance with applicable building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, environmental, and workplace regulations.
Partner with Security, People, Legal, and IT to maintain physical security and workplace safety programs.
Oversee emergency preparedness, evacuation procedures, and facilities-related business continuity planning.
Coordinate required inspections, permits, certifications, and regulatory documentation.
Proactively identify and mitigate facilities-related operational and safety risks.

Partner with leadership to anticipate future space requirements and organizational growth.
Optimize workstations, conference rooms, shared spaces, employee amenities, and sample and fabric library storage.
Coordinate office reconfigurations, furniture installations, and internal moves.
Establish systems to track space utilization, facilities assets, and capital investments.
Develop a multiyear facilities strategy balancing employee experience, operating costs, capacity, and infrastructure reliability.

Build and lead a high-performing facilities organization appropriate for the scale and complexity of the new headquarters.
Directly manage the Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, establishing clear responsibilities, productivity expectations, inventory accuracy standards, and development plans.
Establish operating procedures, performance expectations, and escalation protocols across facilities and library operations.
Implement technology for maintenance management, asset tracking, sample inventory management, vendor oversight, and reporting.
Create a culture of urgency, accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
Establish measurable KPIs and regularly report performance to leadership.

Required
Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive facilities management or corporate real estate operations experience.
5+ years of leadership experience managing large, complex corporate office environments.
Demonstrated experience operating a major corporate headquarters or similarly sophisticated commercial facility.
Direct experience supporting a major headquarters relocation, new building opening, or large-scale office transition.
Strong understanding of commercial building systems, preventive maintenance, workplace services, and life-safety requirements.
Experience developing and managing significant operating budgets and capital expenditures.
Proven success managing complex vendor relationships and service contracts.
Experience leading operational teams with measurable service and inventory accuracy expectations.
Strong project management, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to operate effectively in a rapidly growing organization.
Exceptional attention to detail, responsiveness, and commitment to operational excellence.
Preferred
Experience managing corporate headquarters facilities exceeding 100,000 square feet.
Experience transitioning organizations into substantially larger or more complex headquarters environments.
Background in high-growth technology, e-commerce, consumer products, or retail organizations.
Experience overseeing product sample rooms, fabric libraries, inventory control, or similar operational functions.
Experience establishing facilities operations for newly constructed or renovated commercial buildings.

Knowledge of San Francisco building codes, regulatory requirements, and commercial property operations.

title: Staff Software Development Engineer in Test
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Staff Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET)
We are seeking a highly experienced Staff SDET to join our growing Quality Engineering team. This is a senior technical leadership role focused on designing scalable automation, improving system testability, and setting engineering-wide quality practices. You will combine strong software development skills with deep testing expertise to build frameworks, tools, and infrastructure that help engineering teams deliver reliable, high-quality software at scale. In this role, you will define the SDET and automation strategy across multiple products and teams, influence architecture decisions from a quality perspective, and reduce dependence on manual regression.
Responsibilities:
Define and drive the SDET and test automation strategy across multiple products and engineering teams.
Architect, build, and maintain scalable automation frameworks for UI (app and web), API, integration, end-to-end, and service-level testing.
Develop production-quality test code in Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or C#, and build reusable libraries, utilities, test-data frameworks, and infrastructure.
Design automated testing solutions for microservices, APIs, distributed systems, and mobile and web applications.
Integrate automated test suites with CI/CD pipelines, establish effective quality gates, and improve execution speed, reliability, parallelization, and maintainability.
Identify and eliminate flaky tests, and build solutions for test-data generation, environment management, mocking, service virtualization, and dependency management.
Partner with software engineers and architects during system design to improve testability, reliability, scalability, and observability.
Implement shift-left and continuous testing practices across the software development lifecycle.
Define and monitor engineering quality metrics, including automation coverage, defect leakage, flaky-test rates, execution time, and release quality.
Perform deep debugging and root-cause analysis of complex failures across application, API, database, and infrastructure layers.
Evaluate and introduce new automation tools, frameworks, and engineering practices, and lead technical design reviews.
Mentor SDETs and software engineers on automation architecture, coding standards, and testing best practices, and drive cross-team initiatives that improve engineering quality and developer productivity.
Qualifications
Required:
8+ years of experience in SDET, software engineering, test automation, or quality engineering roles
Strong software development skills in at least one language such as Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or C#, with a solid grasp of object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithms, and software design principles
Proven experience designing automation frameworks from the ground up
Hands-on experience with tools such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, Appium, REST Assured, PyTest, TestNG, JUnit, or equivalent
Strong experience with REST APIs, microservices, and backend or service-level automation
Experience with SQL-based database validation and with testing complex distributed and asynchronous systems
Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Azure DevOps, and proficiency with Git
Strong debugging, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis skills, along with a solid understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and testing methodologies
Demonstrated ability to influence engineering practices across multiple teams
Excellent communication, technical leadership, and collaboration skills
Preferred:
Experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP, and with Docker and Kubernetes
Experience with performance testing tools such as k6, JMeter, Gatling, or Locust
Knowledge of event-driven technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ, and experience with contract testing tools such as Pact
Experience with observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, or Splunk
Understanding of security testing and application security fundamentals
Experience with large-scale SaaS, cloud-native, or enterprise platforms
Experience building internal developer or test productivity tools
Exposure to AI-assisted test generation or AI-based quality engineering tools

A junior advisor can identify an escalating situation and hand it off according to procedure. Brand Ambassadorship: Every advisor is a steward of the Rivian brand. A foundational understanding includes knowledge of our products and a commitment to our values. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary Our data is at the core of our mission. As a Data Engineer at Rivian, you will have an opportunity to learn, build and create data solutions that help Rivian leverage data to be the best at producing the vehicles and software that keep the world adventuring. You will work across engineering teams in various different areas of the business, from Sales, Commercial, People and HR, Facilities, Finance, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing. As a data engineer, you will help us build AI ready data, and help us build and rebuild foundational data in the business areas that help us most to run our business successfully and get our latest vehicle, the R2, in the hands of consumers across the US. You will ingest, standardize, and enrich data with the latest best practices in data modeling, batch/microbatch/real-time data, and AI ready data practices. You will help us build rich context aware data, meta data, dimensional models and data model knowledge graphs for automation and agent use. This position will be located in Atlanta, GA and report to our Sr. Director of Data. Responsibilities Build strong partnerships with data engineers, software engineers working on front line and back end systems, business partners building and maintaining functions across Rivian. Contributing to and shaping data engineering pipelines, tables and platform tools to make the Rivian landscape what it needs to propel into the future. Design, build and contribute to building a data engineering function that makes strong decisions on building batch data pipelines, and building real-time data pipelines, and when to use either. Help build strategic self-service capabilities that enable analysts across different areas to build for the future, and help us achieve our mission. Work with the business to help understand their current and future needs for data, and to unlock capabilities to help them be more efficient. Translate business needs into requirements that you can use to help build a data landscape that goes beyond what the business is asking for and looks to help Rivian scale. Use various AI models, and agents to both unlock productivity and capability for the business Build AI ready semantic data, including data such as knowledge graphs to enable the business lines to build their own efficiencies in using AI. Look across various domains, and build cross domain functionality and knowledge into enterprise data. Qualifications A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or a higher degree (Masters or Phd) is a plus. 12-15 years experience building data-foundation, backend, or data engineering systems, someone other engineers naturally look to for direction. Proficient with writing well structured functional and object oriented code - ideally in Spark and Python. Experience with most modern data stacks end-to-end: ingestion, processing, storage, and serving. You're comfortable making decisions on when to batch data, stream data, or microbatch data and you know the tradeoffs of each. Experience with the latest in AI and agentic technologies as they apply to data engineering, and when to utilize each model or branded model for an optimal outcome. Experience working in a cloud environment, and know how to implement CI/CD components and pipelines. You are also curious about the platform components and how to optimize your pipelines to work with these. Comfortable in complex and fast paced business spaces, prioritizing your own impact and you know how to apply agile and other methodologies to help create transparency, prioritization and efficiency to your work. Go and Python libraries, CLI tools, and Terraform modules that let teams spin up secure, compliant environments with no manual work from us. ● Design chargeback models and cost visibility on Databricks System Tables, and lead architecture reviews with data engineering and ML teams to refactor pipelines (for example, to serverless or event-driven designs) and optimize multi-million dollar budgets. ● Set standards for reliability, SLOs, governance (row and column-level security, ABAC, lineage), and incident response. ● Establish standards for infrastructure as code, Databricks Asset Bundles, and mature GitOps workflows, driving CI/CD improvements through comprehensive testing and strict multi-tier deployments (dev, staging, prod), while raising the technical bar through design and code reviews. ● Build strong partnerships with data engineers, software engineers, security, cloud infrastructure, and business partners who depend on the platform. ● Use AI models and agents to increase your productivity and help build capabilities that let the business use data and AI safely. ● Drive platform security and governance across IAM, secrets management, network isolation, encryption, and audit logging, managing enterprise lineage and metadata via Unity Catalog. ● Build and maintain platform observability, monitoring, and alerting across pipeline health, SLAs, cluster Qualifications ● Decoupled data architectures, and migrating large workloads or reducing vendor dependence at petabyte scale. ● Databricks in depth: architecture (control plane versus data plane, Unity Catalog limits), account and workspace design, System Tables, compute policies, Asset Bundles, and the APIs and SDKs, managed through Terraform and code, not the UI. ● Open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg) and interoperability with external query engines. ● Advanced Python, Go, or Scala, and experience building distributed services, internal developer tools, and infrastructure operators. ● AWS at enterprise scale: multi-account design, Transit Gateway, IAM trust policies, , KMS, and cross-account sharing. ● Apache Spark internals and tuning, and the tradeoffs between batch, microbatch, and streaming at multi-petabyte scale. ● Infrastructure as code (Terraform preferred), CI/CD, GitOps, containers, and zero-downtime updates. ● Observability and governance: metrics, logs, alerting, SLOs, access control (RBAC and ABAC), lineage, auditing, encryption, and secret management. ● A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field, or equivalent experience. A higher degree is a plus. ● Modern data transformation framework administration: managing extensive deployments, CI/CD orchestration, environment isolation, and compute optimization, backed by a solid understanding of the developer experience (data modeling and materializations). ● Analytical and serving infrastructure: operating reporting and application platforms at scale, including provisioning, network routing, access control, and unified catalog integration, with an appreciation for how these applications are built and used. Workload Standardization: Curate and manage centralized deployment manifests and templates used across multiple projects to standardize application delivery to Kubernetes. Containerization: Leverage containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, containerd) to package, distribute, and run applications consistently across all environments. SCM Ecosystem & Platform Architecture Source Control Governance: Oversee Source Code Management (SCM) architecture, ensuring system stability, scalable configuration, and strategic alignment with the broader engineering organization. System Monitoring: Monitor platform performance, troubleshoot system issues, and enforce modern usage practices across all development teams. Continuous Compliance: Embed production readiness checks directly into the CI/CD pipeline to guarantee that deployed apps and services remain compliant over time. Collaboration & Developer Support Engineering Partnership: Act as a strategic partner to development teams, identifying pipeline bottlenecks and providing actionable solutions for build and release challenges. Technical Mentorship: Provide expert guidance on CI/CD best practices, release engineering strategies, and GitOps deployments. Qualifications What You'll Bring Primary Toolchain & Adaptability: Our core in-house tooling utilizes GitLab, GitLab CI, Argo CD, and Helm. However, candidates with strong experience in equivalent systems (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Flux, Kustomize) will absolutely be considered, provided you are highly interested in learning and can quickly master new tooling. Experience: 7–10 years in Platform Engineering, Developer Experience, Build and Release Engineering, or DevOps, supporting large-scale software engineering organizations. DevEx Focus: Proven track record of improving developer productivity, building self-service platforms, and reducing friction in the software development lifecycle. CI/CD & Release Expertise: Proven track record of building complex, automated CI/CD pipelines and leading release management processes. Deep familiarity with enterprise CI/CD platforms and container registries. Kubernetes & Cloud: Hands-on experience with container orchestration platforms (e.g., AWS EKS, GKE, AKS) and cloud operations. Strong background in Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) is highly preferred. GitOps Proficiency: Practical experience with GitOps methodologies and automated Kubernetes deployments. Coding & Scripting: 4–6 years of software development and automation experience. As a Staff-level engineer, you must possess the coding proficiency to architect in-house platform tooling. Strong shell scripting skills (e.g., Bash) are required. Additionally, strong fluency in Go is highly preferred, but experience in comparable systems languages (e.g., Python, Rust, Java, C#) with an appetite to ramp up on Go quickly is acceptable. SCM Administration: Experience overseeing, administering, and scaling enterprise version control systems. Branching Strategies: Familiarity with various branching strategies (e.g., Trunk-based development, GitFlow) to effectively support and optimize the SDLC is a plus. Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.
Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.
This is a remote  position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.

In this role, you will:
Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.
Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.
Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.
Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

Samsara's Go-To-Market AI product team builds the internal products our sellers, customer success managers, and support reps use every day. Functioning much like a general manager with product at the core, this broad leadership role requires you to build, coach, and grow a high-performing team of product managers while driving enablement, cross-functional alignment, and strategic execution.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.
In this role, you will:
Own the strategy, roadmap, and business outcomes for our internal AI-native GTM platform, and be accountable for whether the business adopts it.
Manage the platform as one portfolio, so every part of it shares the same data, intelligence and building blocks, and users get one consistent experience.
Build an AI-native product practice. Take the best of traditional product management, such as PRDs, prioritization, launch readiness and measurement, and reinvent it with AI so the team moves faster and builds better.
Understand internal users' problems and analyze data to identify what to build, sometimes finding the need before users can articulate it.
Write clear requirements and partner closely with engineering, which leads technical implementation, to deliver a high-quality product. Make sure you and your team test the product firsthand.
Keep pace with an engineering team that moves fast and ships at high velocity. Gather input from the field quickly, turn it into a clear direction for engineering, and use AI to shorten the loop from feedback to shipped improvement.
Define what quality means for AI products, including accuracy, trust, evaluation and human review, and hold every release to that bar.
Drive adoption by coaching sellers and partnering with Sales Enablement and Product Marketing, and measure the business impact of what you ship.
Set clear, measurable goals for adoption, productivity and business impact, instrument the product to track them, and use the results to decide what to build next.
Resolve cross-functional dependencies, such as aligning teams on shared datasets with Data Engineering or getting Product Marketing content into the AI knowledge base, and take on the analytics and operational work needed to make the product succeed.
Use AI tools in your own work to build prototypes and mini-apps that engineers can take forward into production, and apply AI to improve how Samsara's go-to-market teams work. Hands-on AI experience is a requirement for this role.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team of product managers.
Minimum requirements for the role:
10+ years of experience in product management, or in strategy and operations roles where you owned a product built with engineering.
5+ years of experience leading, developing and mentoring product managers or product-oriented teams, while staying close to execution.
Demonstrated ownership of an internal or business-facing product, including defining the problem, working with engineering to deliver it, driving adoption and showing measurable business impact.
Hands-on experience with AI, such as building or shipping AI-enabled products, using AI tools in your own work, or prototyping with them.
Strong analytical skills, with examples of using data to identify problems, shape product decisions and measure results.
Technical fluency and ability to establish credibility with engineers.
Strong problem-solving and structured thinking, with a record of driving work to completion across teams and stakeholders.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience owning internal tools or AI products used by sales, customer success or other go-to-market teams.
Familiarity with the systems and data that run a go-to-market organization, such as CRM, forecasting and sales enablement tools.
Experience defining quality, evaluation and trust standards for AI products.
Experience coaching end users and working with enablement teams to get a new tool used.
Experience leading product teams that use AI throughout their own work, from research and requirements to prototyping and launch.
Comfort with fast-changing priorities and with the cross-functional alignment that a company at Samsara's scale requires.

title: Senior Quality Inspector (Mechanical)
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots builds AI-native industrial robot arms deployed at manufacturing facilities across the U.S. In June 2026 we closed a $200M Series C at a $1B valuation, led by RoboStrategy with continued backing from General Catalyst and new participation from the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and that's on you. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in the QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss, leading first article inspections, and making sure the parts going into our robots actually match the drawings they came from.


What you'll do

- Perform GD&T inspection (ASME Y14.5) on mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab, catching deviations before they become problems downstream

- Program and operate CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations to keep quality consistent at scale

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work

- Sit on the Material Review Board to help resolve mechanical nonconformances

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, flagging GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework

- Support 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab area clean, organized, and safe


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5

- Hands-on proficiency with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurement tasks without cutting corners


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies
